definition_zh: 章鱼；八爪鱼
definition_en: a sea creature with a soft round body and eight long arms
core_image: 一只软体海怪蹲在石缝里，八条腕足各自伸向不同方向
scene: 潜水员在岩石缝里看到一团会变色的东西，腕足正缓缓展开。The octopus changed colour and slipped into a narrow gap between the rocks.
sceneCN: 这里 octopus 是「章鱼、八爪鱼」（第 1 个义项：有八个腕足的软体海洋动物）；句意：那只章鱼变了颜色，钻进岩石间的窄缝里。

pos.zh: 章鱼；八爪鱼

derivatives.zh: octo（八）+ pod（足）构成，义为「八腕目动物」，是章鱼的类别名
octopus 去词尾加 -oid（像……的）构成，义为「像章鱼的」
octopus 加 -like 构成，义为「章鱼般的」，常形容伸出多臂的结构

senses.title: The eight-armed sea animal
senses.definition: a soft-bodied sea animal with a large head, big eyes, and eight long arms lined with suckers
senses.definitionCN: 一种身体柔软的海洋动物，头大眼大，有八条长腕足，腕上生有吸盘
senses.example: An octopus can squeeze through a hole the size of a coin.
senses.exampleCN: 章鱼能从一枚硬币大小的孔里挤过去。
senses.why: Greek oktō means eight and pous means foot, so the name simply counts the eight arms of the creature.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 oktō 意为八，pous 意为足，这个名字就是数出这种动物有八条腕足。

senses.title: Its flesh as food
senses.definition: the meat of this animal, cooked and eaten in many coastal cuisines
senses.definitionCN: 这种动物的肉，在许多沿海地区的饮食中被烹煮食用
senses.example: The octopus in the salad was grilled and served cold.
senses.exampleCN: 沙拉里的章鱼是烤好之后冷着端上来的。
senses.why: As with other animals, the name of the creature stands for its flesh on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 和其他动物名一样，动物本身的名字也用来指盘中它的肉。

senses.title: A creature with many grasping arms
senses.titleCN: 比喻：多手多臂的组织或力量
senses.definition: a company, system, or group whose branches reach out in many directions at once
senses.definitionCN: 指分支机构或势力范围同时伸向多个方向的公司、体系或团体
senses.example: Critics call the huge firm an octopus that controls every port.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这家巨头是一只控制着每个港口的章鱼。
senses.why: The eight grasping arms make an easy picture for power that reaches everywhere, so the word is used as a figure of speech.
senses.whyCN: 八条抓人的腕足很容易成为「触角伸向各处」的权力形象，于是这个词被用作比喻。

intro.en: Octopus comes from Greek oktōpous, eight-footed, from oktō, eight, and pous, foot.
intro.cn: octopus 来自希腊语 oktōpous（八足的），由 oktō（八）与 pous（足）构成。

items.en: Oktō means eight, and pous means foot; oktōpous describes an eight-footed animal.
items.cn: oktō 意为八，pous 意为足；oktōpous 形容一种有八足的动物。

items.en: The Greeks also called the creature polypous, many-footed, and Latin kept that older name for centuries.
items.cn: 希腊人也称它为 polypous（多足），这个词在拉丁语中沿用了好几个世纪。

items.en: Scientific Latin adopts octopus from Greek in the eighteenth century as a genus name.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语在十八世纪从希腊语引入 octopus，用作属名。

items.en: English natural history borrows the word in the early nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语博物学在十九世纪初借入这个词。

items.en: Everyday English keeps the Greek -us ending, which causes the debate over octopuses, octopodes, or octopi.
items.cn: 日常英语保留了希腊语词尾 -us，因此产生了复数该写 octopuses、octopodes 还是 octopi 的争论。

note.en: Octopus is a Greek eight-footed name, related to other octo- words and to the everyday names of sea and land creatures.
note.cn: octopus 是来自希腊语的「八足」之名，与其它带 octo- 的词以及海陆动物的日常名称相关。

entries.definition: a flat shape with eight straight sides
entries.definitionCN: 八边形

entries.definition: a musical interval of eight notes
entries.definitionCN: 八度；八度音程

entries.definition: a group name for animals with eight arms, including the octopus
entries.definitionCN: 八腕目动物，包含章鱼

entries.definition: a sea animal with a long body and ten arms
entries.definitionCN: 鱿鱼；乌贼（身体细长、有十条腕）

entries.definition: a flat sea animal that gives out dark ink
entries.definitionCN: 乌贼；墨鱼

entries.definition: a soft sea animal with a bell-shaped body and trailing arms
entries.definitionCN: 水母

entries.definition: a small sea animal fixed to a rock or reef
entries.definitionCN: 水螅体；附着在岩石或礁石上的小海洋生物

normalIntro.en: Octopus counts the eight limbs of the animal: Greek oktō for eight plus pous for foot.
normalIntro.cn: octopus 是在数这种动物的八条腿：希腊语 oktō（八）加 pous（足）。

normal.en: Octopus joins the octo- family with octagon and octave.
normal.cn: octopus 与 octagon、octave 同属 octo- 词群。

normal.en: Octopuses is the regular plural, and octopodes is the Greek plural.
normal.cn: octopuses 是规则复数，octopodes 是希腊式复数。

normal.en: Squid has ten arms, but the octopus has only eight.
normal.cn: 鱿鱼有十条腕，而章鱼只有八条。

normal.en: An octopus squirts ink to escape a predator.
normal.cn: 章鱼会喷墨躲避捕食者。

normal.en: Octo- also gives October, once the eighth month of the Roman calendar.
normal.cn: octo- 还构成 October，它曾是罗马历法的第八个月。

abstract.en: Picture eight long arms curling out of a round jar at once.
abstract.cn: 想象八条长臂同时从一只圆口罐子里伸出来。

abstract.en: Think of a ball of ink thrown into water to hide a body.
abstract.cn: 想象在水里放出一团墨汁，把一个身体藏起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a soft bag of jelly pushing through a keyhole.
abstract.cn: 想象一个软软的果冻袋从钥匙孔里挤过去。

examples.en: The diver watched an octopus hide under a rock.
examples.cn: 潜水员看着一只章鱼躲在岩石下面。

examples.en: Octopuses have very good eyesight and can change colour quickly.
examples.cn: 章鱼视力很好，还能迅速变色。

examples.en: We grilled a small octopus with olive oil and lemon.
examples.cn: 我们用橄榄油和柠檬烤了一只小章鱼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「八爪扑死」——八条爪子一通乱「扑」，就是章鱼；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 希腊语 oktō（八）+ pous（足）→ oktōpous（八足的）→ 现代拉丁语属名 octopus → 英语 octopus，核心义「八条腕足的海兽」。

sensesIntro.en: Octopus starts as the name of the eight-armed sea animal, extends to its flesh as food, and is borrowed for any power that reaches out in many directions.
sensesIntro.cn: octopus 首先是八腕海洋动物的名称，再指其可食用的肉，最后被借用来比喻伸向四面八方的势力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eight long sucker-lined arms spreading out from one soft head.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个柔软的头部伸出八条带吸盘的长腕。

branches.en: The animal itself is the literal name the compound gives.
branches.cn: 动物本身是这个词组字面上直接给出的意思。

branches.en: The living creature also gives its name to the food on a plate.
branches.cn: 这种生物的名字也被用作盘中的食材名。

branches.en: Grasping arms become a picture of power that reaches everywhere.
branches.cn: 抓人的腕足被用来比喻触角伸向各处的权力。

branches.en: Its colour change and grip make it a natural figure for a company.
branches.cn: 它会变色、擅长抓握，这些特征使它成为形容公司的天然比喻。

branches.en: The animal and its meat share one name, as with many sea creatures.
branches.cn: 动物与它的肉共用同一个名字，许多海洋生物都是如此。

intro.en: Octopus is a Greek compound, with octo- for eight and the -pus ending from pous, foot, shared with octagon and octave.
intro.cn: octopus 是一个希腊语复合词，octo- 表示八，词尾 -pus 来自 pous（足），与 octagon、octave 共享词素。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek, not Latin, but Greek oktō and pous were taken into scientific Latin as Octopus and oktopus forms.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自希腊语而非拉丁语，但希腊语的 oktō 与 pous 被科学拉丁语采纳为属名 Octopus。

items.example: The prefix octo- also builds octagon and octave.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 octo- 还构成 octagon 与 octave。

items.example: Pous is the foot root in octopus and tripod.
items.exampleCN: pous 是 octopus 与 tripod 中的「足」词根。

items.example: The ending -pus marks a creature with feet.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -pus 表示一种有足的生物。

items.example: Oktōpous is the Greek source of the name.
items.exampleCN: oktōpous 是这个名称的希腊语来源。

items.meaningCN: 八腕的海洋动物；章鱼属
items.example: Octopus is used as a scientific genus name.
items.exampleCN: Octopus 被用作科学上的属名。

items.example: The suffix -oid forms octopoid.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -oid 构成 octopoid。

items.example: The form -pod appears in octopod and tripod.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -pod 见于 octopod 与 tripod。

items.example: Octopod is the wider category name.
items.exampleCN: octopod 是更宽泛的类别名。

items.example: The suffix -like forms octopuslike.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -like 构成 octopuslike。

latinEntries.meaning: genus name of the eight-armed animal
latinEntries.meaningCN: 八腕动物的属名，来自希腊语
多足的；拉丁语中曾用来指章鱼

definition_zh: 气味；臭味；味道；意味
definition_en: a smell, especially one that is strong or unpleasant
core_image: 一阵看不见的香气从敞开的窗口飘进来
scene: 一进门就闻到若有若无的气味，像旧书和灰尘混在一起。A faint odour of old paper and dust met her at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 odour 是「气味」（第 1 个义项：可以闻到的一般气味）；句意：一进门，一股旧纸和灰尘的淡淡气味便迎面而来。

pos.zh: 气味；臭味；名声

derivatives.zh: 基础词加后缀 -less（没有……），义为「无气味的」
词根 odor 加后缀 -ous（充满……的），义为「有气味的」
前缀 de-（去除）加 odor 再加 -ant，义为「除臭剂」
美式拼写，同 odourless，义为「无气味的」

senses.title: A smell in the air
senses.definition: a smell that can be noticed in the air, whether pleasant or not
senses.definitionCN: 空气中可以被闻到的一般气味，或香或臭
senses.example: The kitchen was full of the warm odour of fresh bread.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房里充满了新鲜面包的温热香气。
senses.why: The Latin noun meant smell itself, so the word began as a neutral name for whatever the nose picks up.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词本义就是「气味」，所以这个词最初是中性看待鼻腔所闻到的一切。

senses.title: A foul smell
senses.definition: a strong and unpleasant smell that makes people want to move away
senses.definitionCN: 浓烈难闻、让人想避开的气味
senses.example: A foul odour rose from the drains in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 院子里下水道冒出一股恶臭。
senses.why: Because unpleasant smells are the ones people talk about most, the neutral sense quietly narrowed towards bad smells.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们谈论最多的正是难闻的气味，这个中性义项便悄悄偏向「臭味」。

senses.title: A suggestion of something
senses.definition: a hint or suggestion of an idea or quality that can be sensed
senses.definitionCN: 可以隐约感知到的某种意味或氛围
senses.example: There was an odour of suspicion in the whole report.
senses.exampleCN: 整份报告里透着一股怀疑的意味。
senses.why: Smell spreads and lingers without being seen, so the word lends itself to qualities you sense rather than see.
senses.whyCN: 气味看不见却四处弥散、久久不散，所以这个词也被用来形容只可感知而不可见的性质。

senses.title: In good odour
senses.definition: in a position of being liked or trusted by other people, used in fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 处于被他人喜欢或信任的地位，用于固定短语
senses.example: He was in good odour with the new management.
senses.exampleCN: 他很受新管理层的信任。
senses.why: People judge a person by the atmosphere around him, as if approval were a scent you could catch.
senses.whyCN: 人们凭一个人身边的气氛来判断他，好像认可是一种可以被闻到的香气。

intro.en: Odour comes from Latin odor, a smell, through Old French, and keeps the Latin sense almost intact in English.
intro.cn: odour 经古法语来自拉丁语 odor（气味），进入英语后几乎原样保留了拉丁语的含义。

items.en: A reconstructed root od- was once thought to mean to smell, though the reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为曾有一个重构词根 od- 意为「闻」，不过这一重构仍存疑。

items.en: Odor means a smell, a scent, or a good name, and gives odorus, a related adjective.
items.cn: odor 意为气味、香气，也可指好名声，并衍生形容词 odorus。

items.en: Odor passes into Old French with the same meaning.
items.cn: odor 以相同含义进入古法语。

items.en: Middle English first uses the word for a smell and also for a reputation.
items.cn: 中古英语最早用它表示气味，也用来表示名声。

items.en: British spelling keeps the u of French, while American English writes odor.
items.cn: 英式拼写保留法语里的 u，美式英语则写成 odor。

note.en: Odour sits in the smell family with odor, odorous, and deodorant, and next to the everyday words scent and stench.
note.cn: odour 属于「气味」词族，与 odor、odorous、deodorant 相邻，也贴近 scent、stench 这类日常词。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same word
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的美式拼写

entries.definition: having a smell, often a strong one
entries.definitionCN: 有气味的，常指气味浓烈的

entries.definition: a substance that removes or hides a smell
entries.definitionCN: 除臭剂，去掉或掩盖气味的用品

entries.definition: the general everyday word for what the nose notices
entries.definitionCN: 指鼻子闻到之物，最日常的说法

entries.definition: a light, usually pleasant smell
entries.definitionCN: 淡淡的、通常好闻的气味

entries.definition: a very strong and horrible smell
entries.definitionCN: 恶臭，极强烈难闻的气味

normalIntro.en: Odour is a Latin smell word that English took whole, so its relatives all carry the idea of scent.
normalIntro.cn: odour 是英语整体借入的拉丁语「气味」词，因此它的同族词都带着「气味」的意思。

normal.en: Latin odor means smell, so odour is almost the same word.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 odor 意为气味，所以 odour 几乎是同一个词。

normal.en: Add -less to get odourless: without any smell at all.
normal.cn: 加上 -less 得到 odourless：完全没有气味。

normal.en: Add de- to odor and you get deodorant, a thing that removes smells.
normal.cn: 在 odor 前加 de- 就是 deodorant，一种除臭的东西。

normal.en: Body odour is the standard phrase for the smell of sweat.
normal.cn: body odour 是表示汗味的标准说法。

normal.en: British English keeps the u in odour, American English drops it.
normal.cn: 英式英语保留 odour 里的 u，美式英语则省略。

abstract.en: Picture a ribbon of steam curling up from a hot bowl and reaching your nose.
abstract.cn: 想象一缕热气从热汤里卷起，飘到你的鼻尖。

abstract.en: Imagine holding your breath while you walk past a blocked drain.
abstract.cn: 想象你屏住呼吸走过一个堵塞的下水道。

abstract.en: Think of a room where something feels wrong though nothing looks wrong.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，看不出问题，却总觉得哪里不对劲。

examples.en: A strange odour drifted from the closed cupboard.
examples.cn: 一股怪味从关着的柜子里飘出来。

examples.en: The cleaning staff sprayed the room to remove the odour.
examples.cn: 保洁人员喷洒了房间以去除异味。

examples.en: Under the new manager he was no longer in good odour.
examples.cn: 在新经理手下，他不再得宠了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧德尔」——欧洲某位德尔先生一身香水味，走到哪里都带着气味；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 odor（气味、香气）→ 古法语 odor → 中古英语 odour → 现代英语 odour／odor，核心义「闻到的气味」。

sensesIntro.en: Odour starts as a neutral smell in the air, narrows to a foul smell, then loosens into a hint of meaning and a fixed phrase about favour.
sensesIntro.cn: odour 先指空气中中性的气味，再窄化为难闻的臭味，之后引申为隐约的意味，并在固定短语里指「受宠」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trail of scent drifting in through an open window.
core.cn: 核心意象：一缕气味从敞开的窗口飘进来。

branches.en: Any smell noticed in the air is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 空气中能闻到的任何气味是基础义项。

branches.en: A foul smell is the narrowed, most talked about sense.
branches.cn: 臭味是窄化后、人们最常谈论的义项。

branches.en: A hint of an idea is the figurative drift.
branches.cn: 隐约的意味是比喻性的延伸。

branches.en: Being in good odour means giving off the right atmosphere.
branches.cn: 处于好气味中，就是散发出对的气氛，因而受到喜爱。

branches.en: A bad smell and a bad feeling both make people wary.
branches.cn: 难闻的气味和不对劲的意味都会让人心生警惕。

intro.en: Odour is built on the Latin smell root odor, with English odourless, odorous, and deodorant around it.
intro.cn: odour 建立在拉丁语「气味」词根 odor 之上，周围有 odourless、odorous 与 deodorant。

latinIntro.en: Latin odor names a smell and also a good name, and gives the adjective odorus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 odor 指气味，也指名望，并衍生形容词 odorus。

items.example: Odor is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: odor 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Odour keeps the Latin vowel of French.
items.exampleCN: odour 保留了来自法语的元音拼写。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous forms odorous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 odorous。

items.example: Odorous describes anything that carries a scent.
items.exampleCN: odorous 形容任何带气味的东西。

items.example: The suffix -less forms odourless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 odourless。

items.example: Odourless gas is hard to notice.
items.exampleCN: 无味的气体很难被察觉。

items.example: The prefix de- marks removal in deodorant.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 在 deodorant 中表示去除。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms deodorant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 构成 deodorant。

items.example: Deodorant is de- plus odor plus -ant.
items.exampleCN: deodorant 由 de- 加 odor 再加 -ant 组成。

definition_zh: 漫不经心的；未经准备的；不客气的；随口；随手
definition_en: not planned or thought about carefully, and often a little rude
core_image: 一只手还插在口袋里，话就已经随口说了出去
scene: 经理当着众人随口评价了她的方案，让她很不舒服。The manager gave an offhand remark about her plan in front of everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 offhand 是「随口说出的」（第 1 个义项：未经准备就说出或做出的）；句意：经理当着所有人的面随口评价了她的方案。

pos.zh: 漫不经心的；未经准备的；不客气的
随口；不假思索地

derivatives.zh: offhand 加后缀 -ed 与 -ly，义为「漫不经心地；随口地」
offhand 加后缀 -ed 构成的同义形容词，义为「未经准备的；不客气的」
offhanded 加 -ness（性质），义为「漫不经心的态度」

senses.title: Said without preparation
senses.definition: said or done at once, without planning or thinking it over first
senses.definitionCN: 没有事先计划或思考就立刻说出或做成的
senses.example: She made an offhand comment that later caused trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 她随口说了一句，后来却惹了麻烦。
senses.why: The image is a hand that acts without the head stepping in, so the word names anything done on the spot.
senses.whyCN: 画面是一只手在脑子介入之前就动了，所以这个词指一切当场脱口而出或随手做出的举动。

senses.title: Cool and careless in manner
senses.definition: behaving in a way that shows little interest or care about other people
senses.definitionCN: 表现出对他人缺少兴趣或关心的态度
senses.example: His offhand reply made her feel unwanted.
senses.exampleCN: 他漫不经心的回答让她觉得自己不受重视。
senses.why: When you act without thinking of others, you look cool and careless, so the word then names that manner.
senses.whyCN: 不考虑他人的随口之举会显得冷淡随意，于是这个词也开始指这种态度。

senses.title: Known well enough to answer at once
senses.definition: so familiar with something that you can give an answer without checking
senses.definitionCN: 对某事非常熟悉，不查就能立刻回答
senses.example: He had offhand knowledge of every station on the line.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这条线上的每个车站都了如指掌。
senses.why: If you can answer offhand, the answer must already be in your hand, so the word also praises easy mastery.
senses.whyCN: 如果你能随口作答，说明答案早已握在手中，所以这个词也能夸人信手拈来。

intro.en: Offhand is a plain English compound of off and hand, first recorded in the middle of the eighteenth century, and unrelated to similar-sounding words.
intro.cn: offhand 是 off 与 hand 组成的英语复合词，首见于十八世纪中期，与发音相近的其他词没有关系。

items.en: Off and hand are both old English words, off meaning away from a place.
items.cn: off 与 hand 都是古英语词，其中 off 表示离开某个位置。

items.en: The compound offhand is first recorded in the 1740s in the sense of at once.
items.cn: 复合词 offhand 在十八世纪四十年代首次记录，意为「即刻、当场」。

items.en: From at once it develops the adjective sense of unpremeditated and then careless.
items.cn: 由「当场」发展出形容词义「未经预谋的」，继而指「漫不经心的」。

items.en: The sense of an answer given without reference to notes is well established.
items.cn: 「不查资料就作答」这一义项也已稳固。

items.en: Modern dictionaries list it as both an adjective and an adverb.
items.cn: 现代词典把它同时列为形容词与副词。

note.en: Offhand sits beside the shortened offhanded family and next to near meanings such as casual, curt, and impromptu.
note.cn: offhand 与简化的 offhanded 词族相邻，也贴近「随意」「简短失礼」「即兴」这些近义词。

entries.definition: the longer adjective built from the same parts
entries.definitionCN: 由相同部分构成的较长形容词

entries.definition: in a way that shows little care
entries.definitionCN: 漫不经心地

entries.definition: the body part at the end of the arm
entries.definitionCN: 手臂末端的手，本词的第二部分

entries.definition: relaxed and showing little interest
entries.definitionCN: 随意的；漫不经心的

entries.definition: short and rather rude in speech
entries.definitionCN: 简短无礼的

entries.definition: done without any preparation
entries.definitionCN: 即兴的；未经准备的

normalIntro.en: Offhand joins off and hand: a hand that works while the mind is elsewhere, so the answer comes out on the spot.
normalIntro.cn: offhand 由 off 与 hand 拼成：手已经动了，心还在别处，所以答案脱口而出。

normal.en: Read it as off plus hand, and the hand moves before you can plan.
normal.cn: 把它拆成 off 加 hand，手在你想好之前就动了。

normal.en: Offhand replies are the ones given without checking a note.
normal.cn: offhand replies 是不查笔记就说出口的回答。

normal.en: The adverb offhandedly marks the careless way of speaking.
normal.cn: 副词 offhandedly 标记那种漫不经心的说话方式。

normal.en: Someone is offhand with guests when they hardly greet them.
normal.cn: 一个人对客人几乎不作招呼，就是 offhand with guests。

normal.en: Compare impromptu: impromptu is neutral and praises quick skill, while offhand often sounds a little rude.
normal.cn: 对比 impromptu：impromptu 中性且略显机智，offhand 常带一点失礼的味道。

abstract.en: Picture a waiter waving off a question with one hand and walking away.
abstract.cn: 想象一位服务员一只手一挥打发你的问题，然后转身走开。

abstract.en: Picture a man answering before the chair has even touched the cushion.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人还没坐下就抢先答了话。

abstract.en: Picture a sailor reciting every port from memory with eyes half closed.
abstract.cn: 想象一位水手半闭着眼睛，凭记忆背出每一个港口。

examples.en: Her offhand greeting made the new neighbours feel unwelcome.
examples.cn: 她漫不经心的招呼让新邻居觉得自己不受欢迎。

examples.en: Do not treat a serious problem with offhand answers.
examples.cn: 不要用随口给出的答复来对待严肃的问题。

examples.en: He seemed offhand about the deadline, yet the work was on time.
examples.cn: 他对截止日期显得漫不经心，可工作还是按时完成了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥夫汉德」——奥夫先生一边摆弄汉子的手，一边随口应付问题；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 off（离开；不在状态）+ hand（手）→ offhand：手不等思考就行动，核心义「不假思索、当场而为」。

sensesIntro.en: Offhand starts with actions taken without thinking, spreads to a cool and careless manner, and ends on answers that come straight from memory.
sensesIntro.cn: offhand 先指不经思考就做出的举动，再扩展到冷淡随意的态度，最后指不查资料、凭记忆脱口而出的回答。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that answers while the mind has not yet spoken.
core.cn: 核心意象：手已经作答，脑子还没开口。

branches.en: Anything said at once is the core sense.
branches.cn: 当场说出的话是核心义项。

branches.en: Careless doing turns into a careless manner.
branches.cn: 不经心的举动演变为漫不经心的态度。

branches.en: Speaking without notes can also display skill.
branches.cn: 不查资料就作答，也可以显出真本领。

branches.en: An offhand remark often feels cool to the person hearing it.
branches.cn: 随口的评论在听者耳中往往显得冷淡。

branches.en: The same easy manner can read as rude or as mastery.
branches.cn: 同一种轻松随意，既可读作失礼，也可读作熟练。

intro.en: Offhand is an English compound, so its parts are free words and English endings rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: offhand 是英语复合词，构成它的部分是独立的词与英语词尾，而不是拉丁语词缀。

latinIntro.en: The parts off and hand come from Old English, not from Latin, so there is no Latin family to list.
latinIntro.cn: off 与 hand 来自古英语而非拉丁语，所以没有可以列举的拉丁语同源词。

items.example: Off marks a hand taken away from care.
items.exampleCN: off 标记一只手脱离了谨慎。

items.example: Hand gives the word its bodily picture.
items.exampleCN: hand 给这个词带来身体画面。

items.example: Offhand is the compound adjective and adverb.
items.exampleCN: offhand 是复合形容词兼副词。

items.example: The suffix -ed builds offhanded.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 offhanded。

items.example: The suffix -ly builds offhandedly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 offhandedly。

items.example: The suffix -ness builds offhandedness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 offhandedness。

items.example: Offhanded is the longer form of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: offhanded 是这一形容词的较长形式。

items.example: Offhandedly marks the careless style.
items.exampleCN: offhandedly 标记漫不经心的语气。

items.meaning: freedom to act as one wishes
items.example: Free hand shows hand in another everyday picture.
items.exampleCN: free hand 用另一种日常画面展示了 hand。

definition_zh: 公职人员；在职官员；任职者
definition_en: a person who holds a public position or an official post
core_image: 一个人把办公室的钥匙，也就是那份职务的印章，握在手里
scene: 每个公职人员都要按期申报自己的收入。Every officeholder must report their income each year.
sceneCN: 这里 officeholder 是「公职人员」（第 1 个义项：担任公职或官方职务的人）；句意：每位公职人员每年都必须申报自己的收入。

pos.zh: 公职人员；在职官员；任职者

derivatives.zh: officeholder 去掉 -er 后加 -ing，义为「担任公职」
构成第一条的语素，义为「办公室；公职」
构成第二条的语素，由 hold 加 -er 构成，义为「持有者」

senses.title: A person in a public post
senses.definition: someone who occupies a position such as a senator, judge, or minister
senses.definitionCN: 占据参议员、法官或部长等职位的人
senses.example: The law applies to every officeholder in the state.
senses.exampleCN: 这条法律适用于该州的每一位公职人员。
senses.why: Office first meant a duty given to someone, so an officeholder is simply the person on whom that duty rests.
senses.whyCN: office 最初指交给某人的职责，因此 officeholder 就是承担这份职责的人。

senses.title: A person elected to the job
senses.definition: a politician who currently holds an elected position and may run again
senses.definitionCN: 目前担任民选职位、可能再次竞选的政治人物
senses.example: No sitting officeholder has lost this seat for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 二十年来还没有现任官员丢掉这个席位。
senses.why: Elections draw attention to whoever already holds the office, so the word often contrasts with a challenger.
senses.whyCN: 选举把注意力集中在已经掌权的人身上，因此这个词常用来与挑战者相对。

senses.title: The holder of any office
senses.definition: anyone who formally holds a post, from a club officer to a corporate director
senses.definitionCN: 任何正式担任职位的人，从协会干事到公司董事均可
senses.example: Each officeholder of the club signs the annual record.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部的每位任职者都要签署年度记录。
senses.why: Once a title marks a duty, the person carrying it is an officeholder, whether the body is public or private.
senses.whyCN: 一旦头衔代表一项职责，承担它的人就是任职者，无论机构是公是私。

intro.en: Officeholder joins office, from Latin officium, a duty, and holder, from the Old English verb hold.
intro.cn: officeholder 由 office 与 holder 合成：office 来自拉丁语 officium（职责），holder 来自古英语动词 hold（持有）。

items.en: Officium means a service, a duty, or a post carried out for others.
items.cn: officium 意为服务、职责，或为他人承担的工作。

items.en: Office arrives in English through Old French, where it names a duty or a church position.
items.cn: office 经古法语进入英语，当时指职责或教会职位。

items.en: The verb hold comes from Old English healdan, meaning to keep or grasp.
items.cn: 动词 hold 来自古英语 healdan，意为持有或抓住。

items.en: Office takes on the sense of a public or official position.
items.cn: office 获得「公共或官方职位」的含义。

items.en: The compound officeholder appears as a neutral name for whoever fills a post.
items.cn: 复合词 officeholder 出现，用来中性称呼填满某个职位的人。

items.en: American political writing uses it widely for selected and elected officials.
items.cn: 美国政治写作广泛用它指被任命和被选出的官员。

note.en: Officeholder belongs to the office word family with officeholder and office, and sits next to official, incumbent, and incumbent nouns.
note.cn: officeholder 属于 office 词族，并贴近「官员」「现任者」等近义词。

entries.definition: a room to work in, or a public position
entries.definitionCN: 办公室，或公共职位，本词的前半部分

entries.definition: a person who has or keeps something
entries.definitionCN: 持有者，本词的后半部分

entries.definition: a person with a position of authority, often in the armed forces
entries.definitionCN: 军官，或担任执法职务的人，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: a person in a position of authority
entries.definitionCN: 官员，常指一般的行政要员

entries.definition: the person who currently holds an elected post
entries.definitionCN: 现任者，强调选举语境

entries.definition: an employee of the state who is not elected
entries.definitionCN: 公务员，非经选举产生

normalIntro.en: Officeholder is built from two common words, office and holder, so the key is to see the post and the person holding it together.
normalIntro.cn: officeholder 由 office 与 holder 两个常用词拼成，记住的关键是把「职位」和「握着它的人」放在一起。

normal.en: Office means a post as well as a room, so an officeholder is not someone in a room but someone in a post.
normal.cn: office 既指办公室也指职位，所以 officeholder 不是坐在房间里的人，而是身在其位的人。

normal.en: Holder comes from hold, so the word means the person who holds the post.
normal.cn: holder 来自 hold，因此这个词指握着这个职位的人。

normal.en: The plural officeholders takes an s with no space.
normal.cn: 复数 officeholders 直接加 s，中间不留空。

normal.en: American news often pairs it with public or elected.
normal.cn: 美国新闻常把它与 public 或 elected 搭配使用。

normal.en: Compare official: official is broader, officeholder stresses the office being held.
normal.cn: 对比 official：official 范围更广，officeholder 更强调被担任的那个职位。

abstract.en: Picture a seal on a desk that only one person is allowed to press.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上有一枚印章，只有一个人有权按下。

abstract.en: Picture a nameplate on a door that can be swapped but never left blank.
abstract.cn: 想象门上的姓名牌可以换人，却从不会空着。

abstract.en: Picture a chair that stays warm while its occupant changes every few years.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子，人每隔几年换一次，椅面却总是热的。

examples.en: Every officeholder must declare any personal interest in the contract.
examples.cn: 每位公职人员都必须申报自己在这份合同中的任何私人利益。

examples.en: The quiet former officeholder refused to comment.
examples.cn: 这位低调的前任官员拒绝发表评论。

examples.en: Local officeholders gathered to discuss the new bus route.
examples.cn: 地方任职者聚在一起讨论新的公交线路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「办公室厚得」——办公室的墙厚得很，因为里面坐着一位公职人员，手握职务；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 officium（职责、服务）→ 古法语 office → 英语 office（职位）+ 古英语 hold（持有）+ -er → officeholder，核心义「持有职位之人」。

sensesIntro.en: Officeholder moves from any public post, to the elected person already in place, to any formal post in any body.
sensesIntro.cn: officeholder 从泛指担任公职的人，扩展到已经当选在位的官员，再泛指任何机构中的正式任职者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal on a desk that only the person in the post may use.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的一枚印章，只有身在其位的人才能使用。

branches.en: Any public post is the central sense.
branches.cn: 泛指担任公职是中心义项。

branches.en: Elected holders are the political narrowing.
branches.cn: 当选的任职者是选举语境的窄化。

branches.en: Any formal post extends the word beyond politics.
branches.cn: 任何正式职位把词义延伸到政治之外。

branches.en: Most elected officials are also public officeholders.
branches.cn: 多数的民选官员同时也是公职人员。

branches.en: Both the candidate and the club officer hold a post.
branches.cn: 候选人与俱乐部干事，都占着一个职位。

intro.en: Officeholder is a compound of office and holder, with -er from hold, and both parts trace back to Latin officium and Old English healdan.
intro.cn: officeholder 是 office 与 holder 的复合词，其中 -er 来自 hold，两部分分别可追溯到拉丁语 officium 与古英语 healdan。

latinIntro.en: The first part comes from Latin officium, a duty, while the second is Germanic through Old English, so the Latin family is thin.
latinIntro.cn: 前半部分来自拉丁语 officium（职责），后半部分经古英语来自日耳曼语，所以拉丁语同源词较少。

items.example: Officium gives office its duty sense.
items.exampleCN: officium 赋予 office「职责」义。

items.example: Office is the first half of the word.
items.exampleCN: office 是这个复合词的前半部分。

items.example: Hold supplies the holding picture.
items.exampleCN: hold 提供「握着」的画面。

items.example: The suffix -er turns hold into holder.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 hold 变成 holder。

items.example: Holder is the second half of the word.
items.exampleCN: holder 是这个复合词的后半部分。

items.meaningCN: 职责或服务性质的词尾
items.example: The ending -office appears in post office and in-office duties.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -office 出现在 post office 等表达里。

items.example: The suffix -holding forms officeholding.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -holding 构成 officeholding。

items.meaning: the state of holding an office
items.example: Officeholding is limited by law in many places.
items.exampleCN: 许多地方以法律限制任职期限。

items.example: Official shares the Latin officium root.
items.exampleCN: official 共享拉丁语 officium 词根。

definition_zh: 离岸的；向海一方的；海上的；设在国外的
definition_en: situated or moving away from the shore, out at sea, or based in another country
core_image: 船头朝外，离开沙滩，驶向深蓝色的大海
scene: 海风很大，平台稳稳立在水面上，工作人员远远望着岸边。The oil platform stands far offshore, beyond the reach of any harbour.
sceneCN: 这里 offshore 是「离岸的、远离海岸的」（第 1 个义项：离开海岸、位于海上）；句意：石油平台远远矗立在离岸的海面上，任何港口都够不到。

pos.zh: 离岸的；海上的；设在国外的
离岸地；向海地

collocations.zh: 离岸风；从陆地吹向海面的风

derivatives.zh: 由 offshore 加 -ing 构成，指「离岸外包；把业务移到海外」
offshore 的过去分词作形容词，指「已外包到海外的」

senses.title: Away from the shore
senses.definition: located or moving away from the land, out at sea
senses.definitionCN: 位于或朝向远离陆地的海上
senses.example: The ferry kept a safe distance offshore.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮保持在离岸的安全距离上行驶。
senses.why: Off- carries the idea of going away, so offshore names the zone that lies away from the shore.
senses.whyCN: off- 带有「离开」的意味，offshore 就指离开海岸之后的那片区域。

senses.title: Blowing from land out to sea
senses.definition: describing wind that blows from the land towards the sea
senses.definitionCN: 形容从陆地吹向海面的风
senses.example: An offshore breeze kept the beach cool all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵离岸风让沙滩整个下午都很凉爽。
senses.why: The same spatial direction, seen from the coast, makes wind that moves seaward an offshore wind.
senses.whyCN: 从海岸看，同一个空间方向使吹向海面的风被称为离岸风。

senses.title: Built or done at sea
senses.definition: describing equipment, drilling, or work that takes place out on the sea
senses.definitionCN: 形容在海上进行的设备、钻井或作业
senses.example: Engineers inspected the offshore rig before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师们在入冬前检查了海上钻井平台。
senses.why: Because offshore land is sea, anything installed there is naturally described as offshore.
senses.whyCN: 既然离岸的「陆地」就是海面，安装在那里的一切自然都叫 offshore。

senses.title: Placed in another country
senses.definition: based in a different country, especially for tax or business reasons
senses.definitionCN: 设在另一个国家，尤指出于税务或商业考虑
senses.example: The company moved its savings to an offshore account.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把存款转移到了境外账户。
senses.why: The word widened from beyond the shore to beyond national jurisdiction, so money held abroad is held offshore.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「海岸之外」扩大到「国家管辖之外」，所以放在国外的钱就是 offshore。

senses.title: Outsourced abroad
senses.definition: describing work given to workers or firms in another country
senses.definitionCN: 形容交给别国工人或公司完成的工作
senses.example: The call centre was outsourced offshore to cut costs.
senses.exampleCN: 这家呼叫中心被外包到海外以削减成本。
senses.why: Business use of offshore makes it the verb-like badge of moving jobs across a border.
senses.whyCN: 商业上的 offshore 让这个词成为「把岗位移出国界」的标志。

intro.en: Offshore is a native English compound of off and shore, first used in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: offshore 是英语本土复合词，由 off 与 shore 组成，首见于十八世纪。

items.en: Off comes from Old English of, meaning away or from.
items.cn: off 来自古英语 of，意为「离开、从」。

items.en: Shore settles into its modern spelling and meaning.
items.cn: shore 的拼写和含义在中古英语时期定形。

items.en: Offshore is first recorded as a nautical description of things away from the land.
items.cn: offshore 首次被记录，用来描写远离陆地的航海事物。

items.en: The word spreads to winds, fishing, and early seabed work.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到风、渔业和早期的海底作业。

items.en: Oil platforms and finance give offshore its technical and financial senses.
items.cn: 石油平台与金融业赋予 offshore 技术义与金融义。

note.en: Offshore sits in the shore family and is flanked by onshore, inshore, and maritime terms.
note.cn: offshore 属于「岸」词族，旁边是 onshore、inshore 以及航海相关的近义词。

entries.definition: on or towards the land
entries.definitionCN: 陆上的；向岸的

entries.definition: close to the shore
entries.definitionCN: 近岸的

entries.definition: the land along the edge of the sea
entries.definitionCN: 海岸；岸边

entries.definition: connected with the sea and shipping
entries.definitionCN: 海事的；航海的

entries.definition: in or to another country
entries.definitionCN: 海外的；国外的

entries.definition: living in the open sea
entries.definitionCN: 远洋的；生活在开阔海面的

normalIntro.en: Off means away and shore means the coast, so offshore is the place that lies beyond the lines of the beach.
normalIntro.cn: off 意为「离开」，shore 意为「海岸」，所以 offshore 就是沙滩线之外的那片地方。

normal.en: An offshore wind blows from the land out to the sea.
normal.cn: offshore wind 是从陆地吹向海面的风。

normal.en: An offshore oil rig is a platform standing in the sea.
normal.cn: offshore oil rig 是立在海水中的钻井平台。

normal.en: Offshore accounts are kept in another country.
normal.cn: offshore account 指存放在另一个国家的账户。

normal.en: Offshore wind farms turn sea breezes into electricity.
normal.cn: offshore wind farm 把海风变成电力。

normal.en: Compare onshore: onshore is land-based, offshore is sea-based.
normal.cn: 对比 onshore：onshore 在陆上，offshore 在海上。

abstract.en: Picture a boat pushing away from the sand into deep water.
abstract.cn: 想象一条船离开沙滩，驶向深水。

abstract.en: Feel a breeze at your back as you face the open sea.
abstract.cn: 想象你面朝大海时，风从背后吹来。

abstract.en: See a steel platform floating on blue water, far from any town.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钢平台漂在蓝水上，远离任何城镇。

examples.en: The island lies about ten miles offshore.
examples.cn: 这座岛离岸大约十英里。

examples.en: Offshore wind farms now supply power to many coastal towns.
examples.cn: 海上风电场如今为许多沿海城镇供电。

examples.en: Regulators are examining how offshore companies handle their funds.
examples.cn: 监管机构正在调查离岸公司如何处理资金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥夫少」——船一离开岸边就少人管，漂在海外；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 off（离开）+ shore（海岸）复合而成，核心义「离开海岸、到海上去」，后引申为「境外的」。

sensesIntro.en: Offshore starts as a spatial word for the sea beyond the coast, then extends to wind direction, sea-based work, and finally money or jobs placed in another country.
sensesIntro.cn: offshore 最初是空间词，指海岸之外的海面，再扩展到风向、海上作业，最后指放在别国的钱或岗位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boat pushing off from the sand into deep water.
core.cn: 核心意象：船从沙滩推开，驶向深水。

branches.en: The literal spatial sense is the everyday use.
branches.cn: 字面的空间义是日常用法。

branches.en: Wind direction borrows the same seaward geometry.
branches.cn: 风向义借用了同一个朝向海面的几何关系。

branches.en: Sea-based work and equipment are the technical sense.
branches.cn: 海上作业与海上设备是技术义项。

branches.en: Finance and outsourcing stretch offshore from sea to borders.
branches.cn: 金融与外包把 offshore 从海面延伸到国界。

branches.en: Both senses treat the sea as the direction or the workplace.
branches.cn: 这两个义项都把海当作方向或工作场所。

intro.en: Offshore is an English compound built from the prefix-like off and the Old English noun shore.
intro.cn: offshore 是由类前缀 off 与古英语名词 shore 构成的英语复合词。

latinIntro.en: Offshore is native English and has no Latin ancestor; related Latin-root words such as marine are listed for comparison.
latinIntro.cn: offshore 是本土英语词，没有拉丁语祖先；marine 等拉丁词根词列出仅供对照。

items.example: Off marks the direction away from a point.
items.exampleCN: off 标出离开某一点的方向。

items.example: Shore names the edge of the land.
items.exampleCN: shore 指陆地边缘。

items.example: Offshore joins the two halves with a hyphen-free spelling.
items.exampleCN: offshore 把两部分合成一个词。

items.example: Onshore uses on in place of off.
items.exampleCN: onshore 用 on 替换了 off。

items.example: Inshore narrows the distance to the coast.
items.exampleCN: inshore 把距离收近到海岸。

items.example: The prefix -like off- builds offside and offset.
items.exampleCN: 类前缀 off- 还能构成 offside、offset。

items.example: The combining form -shore builds seashore and lakeshore.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -shore 能构成 seashore、lakeshore。

items.example: An offshore wind farm is a farm at sea.
items.exampleCN: offshore wind farm 就是海上的风电场。

items.example: An offshore account is an account abroad.
items.exampleCN: offshore account 就是境外的账户。

definition_zh: 药膏；软膏；油膏
definition_en: a smooth, greasy substance that you rub on the skin to heal or soothe it
core_image: 指腹取一坨亮亮的油膏，在皮肤上抹开成薄薄一层
scene: 孩子的膝盖擦破了皮，妈妈从药箱里挤出一团油膏，轻轻抹在伤口上。The doctor told her to put a little ointment on the cut twice a day.
sceneCN: 这里 ointment 是「药膏」（第 1 个义项：抹在皮肤上的软膏）；句意：医生让她每天在伤口上涂两次药膏。

pos.zh: 药膏；软膏；油膏

derivatives.zh: 同源动词，由古法语 enoint 演变，义为「涂油于；用油祝圣」
anoint 加 -ment 构成，义为「涂油礼；敷油」
由 oil 加 -y 构成，义为「油质的；油腻的」，与药膏的质地相关

senses.title: A medicinal salve for the skin
senses.definition: a soft, oily preparation that is rubbed on the skin to treat or soothe it
senses.definitionCN: 涂抹在皮肤上用于治疗或舒缓的柔软油性制剂
senses.example: Apply the ointment to the rash twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 每天在皮疹处涂两次药膏。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to smear with oil, so a greasy preparation smeared on skin became the ointment.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「涂抹油」，所以抹在皮肤上的油性制剂就叫药膏。

senses.title: A protective greasy coating
senses.definition: a greasy layer spread on a surface to protect or lubricate it
senses.definitionCN: 涂在表面上起保护或润滑作用的油层
senses.example: A thick ointment of grease protected the hinges from rust.
senses.exampleCN: 一层厚厚的油膏保护铰链不生锈。
senses.why: Because the substance is defined by being oily and spread on, non-medical uses borrow the same image of protection.
senses.whyCN: 这种物质的本质是油腻并涂抹上去，所以非医学用法也借用了同样的保护意象。

senses.title: Sacred oil of anointing
senses.definition: the holy oil used in religious ceremonies of anointing
senses.definitionCN: 宗教涂油仪式中使用的圣油
senses.example: The priest carried a small jar of ointment into the chapel.
senses.exampleCN: 神父把一小瓶圣油带进了小教堂。
senses.why: Anointing with oil was a sacred act, so the oil itself kept the name ointment in religious contexts.
senses.whyCN: 用油涂抹是神圣的仪式，所以油本身在宗教语境里保留了药膏之名。

senses.title: Soothing words or money
senses.definition: something offered to calm anger or ease hurt feelings
senses.definitionCN: 用来平息怒气、安抚伤害的东西
senses.example: A refund was the ointment they needed to settle the complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 一笔退款正是安抚他们、平息投诉所需要的「药膏」。
senses.why: A remedy for pain became a metaphor for any soothing offer that takes the sting out of trouble.
senses.whyCN: 治疗疼痛的药，喻指任何能减轻麻烦刺痛感的安抚之举。

senses.title: Something that spoils a result
senses.definition: a flaw or fault that spoils an otherwise good outcome
senses.definitionCN: 破坏原本良好结果的瑕疵或过错
senses.example: One careless note was the fly in the ointment for the performance.
senses.exampleCN: 一个粗心的音符成了整场演出里的败笔。
senses.why: The saying about a fly in the ointment gives the word a role as the small thing that ruins something precious.
senses.whyCN: 「药膏里的一只苍蝇」这个说法，让这个词获得「毁掉珍贵之物的小毛病」的角色。

intro.en: Ointment goes back through Old French to Latin unguentum, a noun built on ungere, to smear with oil.
intro.cn: ointment 经古法语上溯到拉丁语 unguentum，该名词由 ungere（涂油）构成。

items.en: Ungere means to smear or anoint with oil.
items.cn: ungere 意为涂抹、给……涂油。

items.en: Unguentum names a salve or oily preparation.
items.cn: unguentum 指软膏、油膏制剂。

items.en: Oignement carries the word into French with the same medical sense.
items.cn: oignement 把这个词带入法语，保持医学含义。

items.en: Ointment appears in Middle English as a common word for salves.
items.cn: 中古英语里 ointment 成为表示软膏的常用词。

items.en: The spellings ointment and unguent still live side by side.
items.cn: 现代英语中 ointment 与 unguent 两种拼写仍然并存。

note.en: Ointment belongs to the salve family through the Latin verb, and near it lie cream, lotion, and plaster.
note.cn: ointment 通过拉丁语动词属于「软膏」词族，旁边是 cream、lotion 与 plaster。

entries.definition: to smear with oil, often in a ceremony
entries.definitionCN: 涂油于；用油祝圣

entries.definition: a soft healing ointment
entries.definitionCN: （同源）软膏；药膏

entries.definition: the small jar that holds salve, often confused in spelling with anointment
entries.definitionCN: 装药膏的小罐；拼写易与 anointment 混淆

entries.definition: a healing substance rubbed on skin
entries.definitionCN: 软膏；药膏

entries.definition: a soft cosmetic or medicinal substance
entries.definitionCN: 乳霜；药霜

entries.definition: a liquid preparation applied to skin
entries.definitionCN: 乳液；洗剂

normalIntro.en: Ointment begins with oint, the same oil sound as anoint, so it is the stuff you smear on with oil.
normalIntro.cn: ointment 开头的 oint 与 anoint 同属「油」的音，所以它就是那种用油涂抹上去的东西。

normal.en: To apply ointment is to spread a salve on the skin.
normal.cn: apply ointment 就是把药膏涂在皮肤上。

normal.en: A tube of ointment is the handiest thing in a first aid kit.
normal.cn: 一管药膏是急救箱里最方便的东西。

normal.en: Antibiotic ointment helps a small cut heal.
normal.cn: 抗生素软膏帮助小伤口愈合。

normal.en: Eye ointment is used overnight for infected eyes.
normal.cn: 眼膏常在夜间用来治疗眼部感染。

normal.en: One fly in the ointment means one small flaw spoils a good thing.
normal.cn: a fly in the ointment 表示一件美事里的小瑕疵。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip lifting a shiny dab of salve from a small jar.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖从小罐里挖出一坨亮亮的药膏。

abstract.en: Feel the smooth greasy film spreading over a sore knee.
abstract.cn: 想象一层滑滑的油膜在酸痛的膝盖上抹开。

abstract.en: See a lantern-lit ceremony where a thumb marks a forehead with oil.
abstract.cn: 想象灯火中的仪式，拇指蘸油在额头抹一下。

examples.en: Nurses apply a cooling ointment to sunburned shoulders.
examples.cn: 护士们在晒伤的肩膀上涂清凉药膏。

examples.en: Keep the ointment away from your eyes.
examples.cn: 药膏要避开眼睛。

examples.en: The only drawback was a missing page, a fly in the ointment.
examples.cn: 唯一的不足是少了一页，正如美中不足。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「油因特闷」——涂上油膏，伤口就不闷了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ungere（涂油）→ unguentum（软膏）→ 古法语 oignement → 英语 ointment，核心义「油性软膏」。

sensesIntro.en: Ointment starts as a greasy healing salve, extends to any protective oily coating and sacred oil, and finally becomes a metaphor for soothing or spoiling.
sensesIntro.cn: ointment 先指油性药膏，再扩展到保护性油层与圣油，最后变成「安抚」或「败笔」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip spreading a shiny film of salve on skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖把亮亮的药膏在皮肤上抹开。

branches.en: The medicinal salve is the core medical sense.
branches.cn: 药用软膏是核心医学义项。

branches.en: Any greasy protective layer borrows the image.
branches.cn: 任何油性保护层都借用了这个意象。

branches.en: Sacred anointing oil grew from the same act of rubbing with oil.
branches.cn: 涂油祝圣所用的圣油来自同一个抹油动作。

branches.en: Soothing offers and spoiling flaws are the figurative pair.
branches.cn: 安抚之举与破坏性的瑕疵构成比喻义的一对。

branches.en: Both a salve and kind words take the sting out of pain.
branches.cn: 药膏和暖心的话都能消除疼痛的刺痛感。

intro.en: Ointment is a loan word from French, with the same Latin root visible in anoint and unguent.
intro.cn: ointment 是从法语借入的词，其拉丁词根在 anoint 与 unguent 中同样可见。

latinIntro.en: Latin ungere means to smear with oil, and unguentum is the oily preparation it produces.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ungere 意为涂抹油，unguentum 是它产生的油性制剂。

items.example: Ungere gives the whole family its oily image.
items.exampleCN: ungere 为整个词族提供油质的意象。

items.example: Unguentum is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: unguentum 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: The Old French form loses the g sound.
items.exampleCN: 古法语形式丢掉了 g 的读音。

items.example: Ointment keeps the medical sense in English.
items.exampleCN: ointment 在英语中保留医学含义。

items.example: The ending -ment marks a substance or result.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 标示一种物质或结果。

items.example: Anoint shares the Latin root but arrives by another route.
items.exampleCN: anoint 共享拉丁词根，却经由另一条路径传入。

items.example: Anointment is the act, ointment is the substance.
items.exampleCN: anointment 是动作，ointment 是物质。

items.example: Unguent is the learned Latin-style twin.
items.exampleCN: unguent 是拉丁风格的书面同源词。

items.example: Oil supplies the texture that ointment needs.
items.exampleCN: 油提供了药膏所需的质地。

definition_zh: 省略；遗漏；疏忽；不作为
definition_en: the act of leaving something out or failing to do something
core_image: 一行清单上有个空位，本来该写的那一项被一把抹掉了
scene: 记者核对新闻稿时发现，报道漏掉了老板的名字。The omission of the director name from the report caused a scandal.
sceneCN: 这里 omission 是「遗漏、省略」（第 1 个义项：把该有的东西舍去或漏掉）；句意：报道中漏掉主管姓名，引发了一场风波。

pos.zh: 省略；遗漏；疏忽；不作为

collocations.zh: 通过不作为；以省略的方式

derivatives.zh: omission 的动词来源，由拉丁语 omittere 经法语传入，义为「省略；遗漏」
由 omit 加 -ive 构成，义为「省略的；漏掉的」
omit 的过去分词作形容词，义为「被省略的；被跳过的」

senses.title: The act of leaving something out
senses.definition: the act of not including someone or something that should be there
senses.definitionCN: 没有把本应包含的人或物写进去的行为
senses.example: The omission of her name from the list was an oversight.
senses.exampleCN: 名单上漏掉她的名字是一次疏忽。
senses.why: Latin omittere means to let something go, so omission is the act of letting a piece drop out of the whole.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 omittere 意为「放开」，所以 omission 就是把某一块从整体里放掉。

senses.title: A thing that is left out
senses.definition: a word, detail, or item that has been left out
senses.definitionCN: 被舍去或漏掉的词、细节或项目
senses.example: Three omissions in the essay cost him marks.
senses.exampleCN: 文章中三处漏写让他丢了分。
senses.why: Once something is let go, it becomes a gap in the record, and that gap is itself called an omission.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物被放掉，就变成记录里的一个空缺，而这个空缺本身也被称为 omission。

senses.title: A failure to do one duty
senses.definition: the failure to do something that you ought to do
senses.definitionCN: 没有做本应做的事
senses.example: His omission to report the fault was later punished.
senses.exampleCN: 他未上报故障，后来因此受罚。
senses.why: By extension, a duty that is let go without being done is an omission of the moral kind.
senses.whyCN: 推而广之，一项本该做却被放掉的职责，就是道德意义上的疏忽。

senses.title: Silent keeping back of information
senses.definition: the deliberate leaving out of important information
senses.definitionCN: 故意不透露重要信息
senses.example: The witness lied by omission and said nothing about the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 证人以隐瞒的方式撒谎，对那次会面只字未提。
senses.why: Keeping a fact back is letting words go unsaid, so silence can be an omission too.
senses.whyCN: 把事实扣住不说，就是让话被放掉，所以沉默也能成为一种省略。

senses.title: Inaction in moral or legal terms
senses.definition: a failure to act that is treated as a fault or even a crime
senses.definitionCN: 被视作过失甚至犯罪的不作为
senses.example: The law punishes omission as well as harmful action.
senses.exampleCN: 法律惩罚不作为，也惩罚有害的行为。
senses.why: When the law treats the inaction itself as the offence, omission turns into a legal charge.
senses.whyCN: 当法律把不作为本身视作违法时，omission 就变成了法律指控。

intro.en: Omission comes from Latin omissio, from omittere, where ob and mittere combine into letting go.
intro.cn: omission 来自拉丁语 omissio，源于 omittere（ob 与 mittere 合成「放掉」之意）。

items.en: Mittere means to send or let go.
items.cn: mittere 意为发送或放开。

items.en: Omittere means to let go or leave out.
items.cn: omittere 意为放开、略去。

items.en: Omissio names the act of leaving something out.
items.cn: omissio 指略去的动作。

items.en: Omission carries the noun into French.
items.cn: omission 把这个名词带入法语。

items.en: English keeps the noun and adds the verb omit.
items.cn: 英语保留了这个名词，并配上了动词 omit。

note.en: Omission belongs to the Latin mittere family, and its nearest meanings are related words for leaving things undone.
note.cn: omission 属于拉丁语 mittere 词族，最近的近义概念围绕「该做而未做」展开。

entries.definition: to leave something out
entries.definitionCN: 省略；遗漏

entries.definition: tending to leave things out
entries.definitionCN: 常漏掉的；省略的

entries.definition: able to be left out
entries.definitionCN: 可以省略的

entries.definition: failure to care for or do something
entries.definitionCN: 疏忽；怠于照管

entries.definition: an accidental failure to notice
entries.definitionCN: 疏忽；无意漏看

entries.definition: the act of keeping something out
entries.definitionCN: 排除；剔除

normalIntro.en: Omission pairs with the verb omit, so both carry the idea of letting a piece drop out of the whole.
normalIntro.cn: omission 与动词 omit 成对，二者都带有「把某一块从整体里放掉」的意思。

normal.en: The omission of a name is a very common clerical error.
normal.cn: 漏写姓名是非常常见的文书差错。

normal.en: A glaring omission jumps out at the reader.
normal.cn: 明显的遗漏一眼就能被读者发现。

normal.en: A sin of omission is a failure to do good when you could.
normal.cn: sin of omission 指能行善时却未行善。

normal.en: Lying by omission hides facts without saying anything false.
normal.cn: lying by omission 不撒谎却把事实藏起来。

normal.en: Compare omission with commission: one is not doing, the other is doing wrong.
normal.cn: 对比 omission 与 commission：前者是不做，后者是做错事。

abstract.en: See a blank slot in a printed list where a name should be.
abstract.cn: 想象打印名单上本该有名字的地方空着一块。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifting one word out of a sentence and dropping it on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把句子里一个词挑出来丢到地上。

abstract.en: Feel the pause when a witness stops just before a dangerous fact.
abstract.cn: 想象证人在关键事实证明前突然停下的沉默。

examples.en: The report was criticized for its omission of key evidence.
examples.cn: 这份报告因遗漏关键证据而受到批评。

examples.en: Several omissions in the form delayed the application.
examples.cn: 表格上的几处漏填延误了申请。

examples.en: In law, omission can be as serious as a deliberate act.
examples.cn: 在法律上，不作为与故意行为可能同样严重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，蜜身受」——漏掉的总是最受益的那部分；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ob-（朝向、加于）+ mittere（送、放出）→ omittere（放掉、略去）→ omissio → 英语 omission，核心义「把某物放掉、不包含」。

sensesIntro.en: Omission begins with the act of leaving something out, then names the missing item itself, and finally extends to duties and disclosures that are not carried out.
sensesIntro.cn: omission 先指「舍去、漏掉」的动作，再指被漏掉的那一项，最后扩展到该履行而不履行的职责与披露。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blank slot in a list where one item should be.
core.cn: 核心意象：清单上本该有一项的位置空着。

branches.en: The act of leaving out is the central sense.
branches.cn: 「舍去」的动作是核心义项。

branches.en: The missing item is the concrete result of that act.
branches.cn: 被漏掉的那一项是该动作的具体结果。

branches.en: A duty not done is an omission in moral terms.
branches.cn: 未履行的职责在道德上就是一种疏忽。

branches.en: Withholding facts and legal inaction are the social and legal senses.
branches.cn: 隐瞒事实与法律上的不作为是社会义与法律义。

branches.en: Both the act and the result are called omissions in everyday use.
branches.cn: 日常用法中动作和结果都称作 omission。

intro.en: Omission is built on the Latin sending root mittere, with the prefix ob-, and is closely tied to the English verb omit.
intro.cn: omission 建立在拉丁语「送」的词根 mittere 与前缀 ob- 之上，并与英语动词 omit 紧密相连。

latinIntro.en: Latin omittere means to let go or leave out, and omissio is its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 omittere 意为放开、略去，其名词形式是 omissio。

items.example: Mittere gives the family its sending image.
items.exampleCN: mittere 为词族提供发送的意象。

items.example: The prefix ob- bends mittere towards leaving aside.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ob- 使 mittere 转向「放到一边」。

items.example: Omittere is the direct parent of omit.
items.exampleCN: omittere 是 omit 的直接来源。

items.example: Omissio gives the English noun its form.
items.exampleCN: omissio 赋予英语名词词形。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的后缀
items.example: The ending -ion turns verbs into nouns of action.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 把动词变成动作名词。

items.example: Omit is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: omit 是简短的英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms omissive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 omissive。

items.example: Omissible adds -ible to the omit stem.
items.exampleCN: omissible 在 omit 词干后加 -ible。

items.meaning: the act of doing, often wrongly
items.example: Commission contrasts with omission in law.
items.exampleCN: 在法律上 commission 与 omission 形成对照。

definition_zh: 猛攻；袭击；大量涌入；猛烈抨击
definition_en: a fierce, sustained attack on someone or something, or a sudden rush of many things at once
core_image: 一大群人顶着盾牌猛冲过河，冲上城门的整个画面
scene: 两个小队在河岸边对峙，冲锋的一方冲上来。The defenders could not hold the gate against the onslaught of the raiders.
sceneCN: 这里 onslaught 是「猛攻」（第 1 个义项：对人或地点的持续猛烈进攻）；句意：守军抵挡不住劫掠者对上城门的猛攻。

pos.zh: 猛攻；袭击；大量涌入；猛烈抨击

derivatives.zh: 由同根动词构成，义为「杀死；杀害」，核心仍是猛烈击打
古旧拼写与非标准拼法，义为「打击；猛攻」，是 onslaught 的词干形式
近义构词联想的名词，义为「交叉火力」，表示攻击从两侧同时压来

senses.title: A violent attack on a place or army
senses.definition: a fierce and usually sustained attack by an army or a crowd against a place or a group
senses.definitionCN: 军队或人群对地点或群体发起的猛烈且往往持续的进攻
senses.example: The fort fell after a three-day onslaught.
senses.exampleCN: 猛攻三天后堡垒失守。
senses.why: The word was first used of cavalry striking a body of troops, so the core is a charge that does not let up.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初用来描述骑兵冲击一支部队，所以核心是不断压上的冲锋。

senses.title: A strong verbal or written assault
senses.definition: a harsh and sustained attack on an idea, a proposal, or someone by speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 用言语或文字对某个观点、提议或某人发起的持续猛烈攻击
senses.example: The plan met with a sudden onslaught from local residents.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划遭到当地居民的突然猛烈抨击。
senses.why: Once the physical charge was in place, speakers simply moved the same force onto words.
senses.whyCN: 身体的冲锋定型之后，人们把同一股力量直接搬到了语言上。

senses.title: A sudden overwhelming amount of something
senses.definition: a very large number of things arriving or coming at once, so that they are hard to deal with
senses.definitionCN: 大量事物同时涌来，多到难以应对
senses.example: The shop could not handle the onslaught of orders.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店应付不了汹涌而来的订单。
senses.why: An attack that overwhelms by force turns easily into a flood that overwhelms by quantity.
senses.whyCN: 靠武力压倒的攻击，很容易转成靠数量压倒的洪流。

senses.title: The first impact of a charge
senses.definition: the crashing blow delivered by a charging body, an older and more physical use
senses.definitionCN: 冲锋者撞出的一下重击，是较早的身体性用法
senses.example: The gate shuddered under the first onslaught.
senses.exampleCN: 城门在第一次撞击下震动。
senses.why: The second part of the word meant a blow, so the noun can name the single impact itself.
senses.whyCN: 词的后半部分本就意为「一击」，所以名词也能直接指那一下撞击。

senses.title: A heavy burden of difficult events
senses.definition: a series of hard events that come at someone one after another, like blows
senses.definitionCN: 一连串接连而来的艰难事件，像一记记打击一样压向某人
senses.example: After losing his job, he faced an onslaught of bills.
senses.exampleCN: 失业之后，他面对接踵而至的账单。
senses.why: The image of repeated blows makes the word fit a run of misfortunes as well as a run of enemies.
senses.whyCN: 「反复击打」的画面让这个词既能用在敌人身上，也能用在一连串不幸上。

intro.en: Onslaught joins English on, meaning onward, with a root that descends from the Old English noun sleaht, a blow. The whole word is English, not Latin.
intro.cn: onslaught 由表示「向前」的英语 on 与源自古英语名词 sleaht「一击」的词干合成，整词是英语本土词，不来自拉丁语。

items.en: Sleaht was a blow or a struck person, and verb forms such as slean meant to strike.
items.cn: 古英语 sleaht 指一击或被击倒的人，slean 等动词形式意为打击。

items.en: The forms slauht and slagt trimmed the ancient cluster and name the striking itself.
items.cn: 中古英语的 slauht 与 slagt 简化了古旧的辅音组合，指「击打」这个动作。

items.en: Scots slaugh meant a battle slaughter, and its spelling was later remade toward slaughter.
items.cn: 苏格兰语 slaugh 指战场上的屠杀，它的拼写后来被向 slaughter 靠拢改写。

items.en: English added the prefix on, onward, to make onslaught, a charge on or against a body of troops.
items.cn: 英语加上前缀 on「向前」，构成 onslaught，指冲向一支部队的进攻。

items.en: The modern spelling onslaught settled in writing and ousted the older onslaught and anslought.
items.cn: 现代拼写 onslaught 在书面上固定下来，取代了较早的 onslaught 与 anslought。

items.en: Modern English extends the charge from armies to criticism, orders, and any overwhelming rush.
items.cn: 现代英语把这场冲锋从军队扩展到批评、订单和任何铺天盖地的涌入。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same on- start or the same striking stem; the near-meaning group separates a charge, a verbal attack, and a flood of things.
note.cn: 形近组收集同样以 on- 开头或同属「击打」词干的词；近义组则把冲锋、言辞攻击和事物洪流分开。

entries.definition: the beginning of something unpleasant, or an attack in older use
entries.definitionCN: 不愉快之事的开始，旧时也指进攻；与 onslaught 同用 on- 前缀

entries.definition: a strong forward rush of people or things
entries.definitionCN: 人或物向前猛冲；与 onslaught 同用 on- 前缀

entries.definition: the killing of many people or animals
entries.definitionCN: 大量屠杀人或牲畜；词干与 sleaht「一击」同源，但与拉丁语无关

entries.definition: a violent attack, especially one sudden in its impact
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈的攻击，尤指一下就打过来的那种；与 onslaught 相比更强调突然的一击

entries.definition: a fast forward rush of troops against an enemy
entries.definitionCN: 军队向敌方快速冲去；与 onslaught 相比更像一次性的冲刺动作

entries.definition: a continuous heavy attack, or a flood of questions and criticism
entries.definitionCN: 持续不断的猛烈攻击，也指连番的质问与批评；比 onslaught 更强调不间断

normalIntro.en: Onslaught is English on plus an ancient blow-stem, so think of something rushing onward at you in one long strike.
normalIntro.cn: onslaught 是英语的 on 加上古老的「击打」词干，所以可以记成一股力量朝你一路压来、久久不停的一次重击。

normal.en: The prefix on- means onward, as in onrush and onset.
normal.cn: 前缀 on- 意为「向前」，onrush 与 onset 都是如此。

normal.en: The stem is linked to Old English sleaht, a blow.
normal.cn: 词干与古英语 sleaht「一击」相关。

normal.en: The usual pattern is an onslaught on or against something.
normal.cn: 常见句式是 an onslaught on 或 against something。

normal.en: Verbs that fit it are survive, resist, and launch.
normal.cn: 常与 survive、resist、launch 等动词搭配。

normal.en: Compare attack: an attack may fail in a minute, an onslaught keeps coming.
normal.cn: 对比 attack：attack 可能一分钟就失败，onslaught 却持续压上来。

abstract.en: Picture a wave that hits the gate again and again before it cracks.
abstract.cn: 想象一道浪反复拍打城门，直到把它撞开。

abstract.en: Hear a stream of newspaper headlines all shouting the same criticism.
abstract.cn: 听一串报纸标题齐声喊出同样的批评。

abstract.en: Imagine an inbox filling faster than you can open the messages.
abstract.cn: 想象收件箱堆得比你打开的还快。

examples.en: The village survived the onslaught of the winter storms.
examples.cn: 村子挺过了冬季风暴的猛烈袭击。

examples.en: Her article launched an onslaught on the new exam system.
examples.cn: 她的文章对新考试制度发起了猛烈抨击。

examples.en: The staff struggled to answer the onslaught of calls.
examples.cn: 员工们忙于应付涌来的电话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「on 加 斯劳特」——一群人 on 着「斯劳特」一路向前，像冲锋一样压过来，就是猛攻 onslaught；这只是连带联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 on（向前）＋古英语 sleaht（一击）的词干 → onslaught（冲向部队的进攻，十六至十七世纪）→ onslaught（十八世纪起定型），核心义「持续压上的猛击」。

sensesIntro.en: Onslaught starts as a charge that keeps coming, then moves onto words, then onto sheer quantity, and finally onto repeated blows in a life.
sensesIntro.cn: onslaught 先指一路压上的冲锋，再转到言辞上，再转到纯粹的数量，最后转到人生中接连而来的打击。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd charging through the water and up against the gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一大群人涉水冲上来，直扑城门。

branches.en: The military charge on a place or an army.
branches.cn: 对地点或军队的军事冲锋。

branches.en: The same force moved onto words and papers.
branches.cn: 同样的力量转到言语和文章上。

branches.en: A charge by quantity instead of force.
branches.cn: 用数量而不是武力发起的冲击。

branches.en: The single crashing impact of a charge.
branches.cn: 冲锋撞出的那一下重击。

branches.en: Repeated blows recast as a run of hard events.
branches.cn: 反复的击打被改写成一连串艰难事件。

intro.en: Onslaught is a home-grown English compound: the prefix on- plus the blow-stem seen in older slaught and in slaughter.
intro.cn: onslaught 是英语本土合成的复合词：前缀 on- 加上见于旧拼写 slaught 与 slaughter 的「击打」词干。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin layer here, because the whole word is native English; the nearest learned relatives come through other roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语层，整词都是英语本土词；书面上最接近的近义词来自其他词根。

items.exampleCN: 猛攻；猛冲；开始

items.example: onslaught, slaught
items.exampleCN: 猛攻；打击（旧拼写）

items.example: slay, slaying
items.exampleCN: 杀死；杀戮

items.example: slaughter, onslaught
items.exampleCN: 屠杀；猛攻

items.example: assail, assault
items.exampleCN: 攻击；袭击

items.example: barrage, volley
items.exampleCN: 弹幕；齐射

items.meaning: a long surrounding attack on a place
items.example: siege, blockade
items.exampleCN: 围攻；封锁

items.meaning: a burst of shots or remarks
items.example: volley, salvo
items.exampleCN: 齐射；齐放

definition_zh: 向前；继续下去；从……起往后
definition_en: forward in space or time, and continuing from a stated point
core_image: 一个人沿着同一条路一直往前走，脚下没有停下的箭头
scene: 列车到站后重新启动，车窗外的田野慢慢退后。The train moved onwards through the fields as the rain began.
sceneCN: 这里 onwards 是「向前、继续前进」（第 1 个义项：空间上一直向前）；句意：列车在雨中继续穿过田野向前行驶。

pos.zh: 向前；继续下去；从……起往后

collocations.phrase: from the start of the term onwards

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词性 -s 构成的基础形式，义为「向前；继续向前的」，也作定语形容词
与 onwards 共用 on- 前缀，加表示冲击的 -rush 构成，义为「猛冲；汹涌而至」
与 onwards 共用 on- 前缀，加 coming 构成，义为「迎面而来的」

senses.title: Forward in space
senses.definition: in a direction further forward, used of walking, travelling, or marching
senses.definitionCN: 朝更前方的方向，多用于行走、旅行或行军
senses.example: The climbers pressed onwards despite the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者冒着大雪继续向前。
senses.why: The word is built from onward, forward, so the physical movement forward is the oldest and most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是在表示「向前」的 onward 之上加副词性 -s 形成的，因此身体上的向前是最古老、最本义的义项。

senses.title: On from a point in time
senses.definition: used after from to mean starting at a certain time and continuing later
senses.definitionCN: 置于 from 之后，表示从某个时间点开始并往后延续
senses.example: From next term onwards, the library will stay open until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 从下学期起，图书馆将开放到午夜。
senses.why: The same forward motion is simply measured on a line of time, which is why from then onwards is the everyday pattern.
senses.whyCN: 同样的向前运动被放到时间线上度量，所以 from then onwards 成了日常固定说法。

senses.title: Continuing without stopping
senses.definition: used of progress, work, or life that keeps going after a pause or a setback
senses.definitionCN: 用于暂停或受挫之后仍不断发展、工作或生活下去
senses.example: After the injury, she rebuilt her career and moved onwards.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤之后她重建事业，继续向前。
senses.why: Movement forward in place suggests advance in effort, so the word comes to mean pushing on rather than turning back.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的向前移动暗示努力上的推进，于是这个词变成「坚持推进」而不是「回头」。

senses.title: Used in set congratulation phrases
senses.definition: in the phrase onwards and upwards, used to wish someone success and improvement
senses.definitionCN: 用于 onwards and upwards 这一祝贺套语，祝愿某人成功并不断进步
senses.example: You have a new job, so onwards and upwards.
senses.exampleCN: 你有了新工作，那就步步高升吧。
senses.why: The upward direction turns plain forward motion into a wish, so the pair became a cheerful formula.
senses.whyCN: 向上的方向把单纯的向前变成一种祝愿，这组词就成了欢快的套语。

senses.title: In headings and route notices
senses.definition: used in travel and map language to show that a vehicle or route continues further ahead
senses.definitionCN: 在交通与地图语言中表示车辆或路线继续通往前方
senses.example: Passengers for the coast should travel onwards from Bristol.
senses.exampleCN: 前往海滨的乘客应在布里斯托尔换乘继续前行。
senses.why: Transport notices need a short word for continuing the journey, and onwards fits the length of a sign.
senses.whyCN: 交通告示需要一个简短词表示「继续行程」，onwards 的长度正好适合标牌。

intro.en: Onwards is English onward with the adverbial -s that also appears in towards and afterwards; onward itself is on plus the suffix -ward.
intro.cn: onwards 是英语 onward 加表示副词性的后缀 -s 构成，towards、afterwards 也是这种 -s；onward 本身则是 on 加后缀 -ward。

items.en: Old English used onweard for facing onward, joining on with the direction suffix weard.
items.cn: 古英语用 onweard 表示「朝前的」，是把 on 与方向后缀 weard 接在一起。

items.en: Middle English onward kept the forward meaning for movement and for time.
items.cn: 中古英语 onward 保留「向前」之义，既用于空间也用于时间。

items.en: Writers added -s to many directional words, giving onwards, towards, and afterwards.
items.cn: 书写者给许多方向词加上 -s，形成 onwards、towards 与 afterwards。

items.en: Onwards appears in print as a common adverb of continuing motion and continuation in time.
items.cn: onwards 在书面中成为常用副词，表示持续运动与时间上的延续。

items.en: Modern usage keeps onwards as the usual British adverb and onward as the usual American and attributive form.
items.cn: 现代用法以 onwards 为英式常用副词，以 onward 为美式与定语常用形式。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the direction-word family built with -ward and -wards; the near-meaning group separates continuing, advancing, and ever-turning words.
note.cn: 形近组展示由 -ward 与 -wards 构成的方向词族；近义组则把「延续」「推进」与「不断旋转」的词分开。

entries.definition: forward, or moving forward
entries.definitionCN: 向前的；继续向前的；onwards 去掉 -s 的基础形式

entries.definition: in the direction of
entries.definitionCN: 朝……方向；与 onwards 同用副词性后缀 -s

entries.definition: toward a higher place or amount
entries.definitionCN: 向上；数量上往高处；与 onwards 同用副词性后缀 -s

entries.definition: toward the front or the future
entries.definitionCN: 朝前或朝未来；比 onwards 更中性，不带「一直坚持」的味道

entries.definition: in front or in the future
entries.definitionCN: 在前方或将来；侧重位置在前，而 onwards 侧重持续前进

entries.definition: from one end of something toward the other
entries.definitionCN: 沿着某物朝另一端；强调沿路线移动，不强调继续

normalIntro.en: Onwards is on plus the direction suffix -ward plus the adverb -s, so it literally wears forward motion on its sleeve.
normalIntro.cn: onwards 是 on 加方向后缀 -ward 再加副词 -s，等于把「向前」写在了身上。

normal.en: The core is on plus -ward, a direction suffix as in backward.
normal.cn: 核心是 on 加方向后缀 -ward，backward 也是这么来的。

normal.en: The -s is the same adverb marker as in towards and afterwards.
normal.cn: 词尾的 -s 与 towards、afterwards 中的副词标记相同。

normal.en: The usual time pattern is from then onwards.
normal.cn: 时间上的常用句式是 from then onwards。

normal.en: It often follows verbs such as move, travel, and press.
normal.cn: 它常跟在 move、travel、press 这类动词之后。

normal.en: British English likes onwards as an adverb, American English usually writes onward.
normal.cn: 英式英语作副词常用 onwards，美式英语通常写 onward。

abstract.en: Picture footprints that continue straight on past the edge of the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一串脚印一直向前，越过了纸页的边缘。

abstract.en: Draw a timeline with a point marked here and an arrow running past it.
abstract.cn: 画一条时间线，标出一个点，再画一支越过它的箭头。

abstract.en: Think of a cyclist standing up on the pedals just to keep climbing.
abstract.cn: 想象骑车的人站起来蹬踏板，只为继续往上爬。

examples.en: From January onwards, the team will meet every Friday.
examples.cn: 从一月起，团队每周五开会。

examples.en: The hikers walked onwards until the light failed.
examples.cn: 徒步者一直向前走，直到天色变暗。

examples.en: She finished the report and moved onwards to the next task.
examples.cn: 她写完报告，接着去做下一项任务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「昂沃兹」——想象一个人「昂」着头，一路「wards」朝前逛，脚步不停，就是「向前、继续」的意思；这只是谐音拆分联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 on「在……上、向前」＋方向后缀 -weard → 中古英语 onward → 十五世纪加副词性 -s 成 onwards，核心义「朝着前方、不停向前」。

sensesIntro.en: Onwards begins as forward motion in space, is measured on a line of time, extends to steady progress, and survives in congratulation and travel formulas.
sensesIntro.cn: onwards 从空间上的向前开始，被放到时间线上度量，再扩展到稳步推进，最后留在祝贺语与交通用语里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone walking the same road forward without turning back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人沿着同一条路一直往前走，不回头。

branches.en: Forward motion with the feet and wheels.
branches.cn: 靠脚与车轮实现的向前移动。

branches.en: The same motion drawn on a timeline.
branches.cn: 同样的运动被画在时间线上。

branches.en: Carrying on after a pause or setback.
branches.cn: 停顿或受挫之后继续前进。

branches.en: Forward plus upward turned into a wish.
branches.cn: 向前加上向上，变成一句祝愿。

branches.en: The same word trimmed for signs and timetables.
branches.cn: 同一个词被压缩进标牌与时刻表。

intro.en: Onwards is built entirely from English pieces: the preposition on, the direction suffix -ward, and the adverbial -s.
intro.cn: onwards 完全由英语语素构成：介词 on、方向后缀 -ward 与副词性后缀 -s。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in this word, because it grew from Old English onweard rather than from a Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语成分，因为它源自中古以前的 onweard，而不是某一拉丁词根。

definition_zh: 不透明的；浑浊的；晦涩难懂的；看不清的
definition_en: not able to be seen through, and hence hard to understand or unclear
core_image: 一扇磨砂玻璃窗，外面的光线透得进来，东西却看不清楚
scene: 浴室的门装的是磨砂玻璃，站在门口看不清里面。The bathroom door is opaque, so nobody could see inside.
sceneCN: 这里 opaque 是「不透明的」（第 1 个义项：光线透不过、看不清后面的东西）；句意：浴室门是不透明的，所以谁也看不见里面。

pos.zh: 不透明的；浑浊的；晦涩难懂的；看不清的
（摄影中的）不透光胶片；（作品的）难懂

derivatives.zh: opaque 加 -ity 构成，义为「不透明性；晦涩」
opaque 加 -ly 构成，义为「不透明地；晦涩地」

semi-「半」加 opaque 构成，义为「半透明的」

senses.title: Not letting light pass through
senses.definition: made of a material that light cannot pass through, so objects behind it cannot be seen
senses.definitionCN: 由光线无法穿透的材料制成，因此看不见后面的物体
senses.example: The bottle is opaque, so the liquid inside cannot be seen.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶子是不透明的，所以看不见里面的液体。
senses.why: The Latin verb opacare meant to darken or shade, so the earliest image is a surface that blocks the light.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 opacare 意为「使暗、遮住」，因此最早的画面就是一挡住光的表面。

senses.title: Cloudy or dark rather than clear
senses.definition: cloudy, milky, or darkened, used of a liquid, a gem, the eye, or the air
senses.definitionCN: 浑浊、发白或变暗，用于液体、宝石、眼睛或空气
senses.example: The old mirror has become opaque over the years.
senses.exampleCN: 那面旧镜子这些年变得浑浊了。
senses.why: A shaded surface is also a cloudy one, so anything that has lost its clarity can be called opaque.
senses.whyCN: 被遮住的表面同时也是浑浊的表面，所以任何失去清澈的东西都可以叫 opaque。

senses.title: Hard to understand
senses.definition: said of writing, speech, or reasoning that is so unclear that it barely lets meaning through
senses.definitionCN: 形容文字、言辞或推理过于含混，几乎不让人看出意思
senses.example: The contract was written in unusually opaque language.
senses.exampleCN: 这份合同用的语言晦涩得出奇。
senses.why: Meaning travels in language much as light travels through glass, so opaque text is text you cannot see into.
senses.whyCN: 意义靠语言传递，就像光靠玻璃透过，因此 opaque 的文字就是看不进去的文字。

senses.title: Not open to inspection
senses.definition: said of organisations or decisions whose workings outsiders can never examine
senses.definitionCN: 形容外人永远查不清其运作方式的机构或决定
senses.example: Voters complained that the funding process was opaque.
senses.exampleCN: 选民抱怨拨款程序不透明。
senses.why: A body that cannot be seen into is figuratively opaque, so the word now names secrecy as well as darkness.
senses.whyCN: 从外面看不进去的机构在比喻上就是不透明的，所以这个词现在既指暗，也指不公开。

senses.title: The opaque noun kinds
senses.definition: in photography, opaque paper used to block light, or in plural, the hardest parts of a text
senses.definitionCN: 摄影中指用于挡光的不透明纸，复数形式则指文章中最难懂的部分
senses.example: The photographer cut a shape from the opaque to mask the lens.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师从不透光纸上剪出一个形状来遮镜头。
senses.why: The adjective froze into a noun wherever the blocked light was a physical sheet, and printers kept the habit.
senses.whyCN: 当被挡住的光就对应一张实物纸时，形容词就冻结成了名词，印刷与摄影业保留了这个习惯。

intro.en: Opaque comes from Latin opacus, shady or dark, and its verb opacare, to darken. English borrowed the form from French, where the final consonant was voiced.
intro.cn: opaque 来自拉丁语 opacus「有阴影的、暗的」及其动词 opacare「使暗」。英语经由法语借入这个词形，法语的词尾辅音是浊音。

items.en: Latin opacus described places in shade, dense woods, and things that block light.
items.cn: 拉丁语 opacus 形容处在阴影中的地方、茂密的树林与挡光的东西。

items.en: The verb opacare meant to make dark or to shade, and turned the adjective into an action.
items.cn: 动词 opacare 意为「使变暗、遮蔽」，把形容词转化成了一个动作。

items.en: Old and Middle French opaque, later also spelled opacque, carried the form onward with a voiced ending.
items.cn: 古法语与中古法语 opaque（后来也拼作 opacque）把这个词形继续带下去，词尾是浊音。

items.en: Early English spells it opak or opake, still chiefly meaning dark or shaded.
items.cn: 早期英语拼作 opak 或 opake，主要仍表示「暗的、有阴影的」。

items.en: Seventeenth-century writers restored a French-style -que spelling, which became standard.
items.cn: 十七世纪的书写者恢复法语式的 -que 拼写，这种写法成为标准。

items.en: Science then fixed the word on light that cannot pass through, and after that on meaning that cannot pass through.
items.cn: 此后科学用法把它固定在「光线无法透过」上，再往后又固定在「意思无法传达」上。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely sound or look close; the near-meaning group moves from unclear liquid to unclear meaning to near invisibility.
note.cn: 形近组只收集读音或拼写接近的词；近义组则从浑浊的液体走到含混的意思，再到近乎看不见。

entries.definition: the state of not letting light through, or of being hard to understand
entries.definitionCN: 不透光、难以看懂的性状；由 opaque 加 -ity 构成的同根名词

entries.definition: to become or make something opaque
entries.definitionCN: 使变得不透明；由同一词干 opac- 加 -ify 构成的动词

entries.definition: not clearly seen or understood
entries.definitionCN: 看不清或难理解的；与 opaque 意思接近，但词源不同，只是读起来相近

entries.definition: full of cloud or not clear, as with water
entries.definitionCN: 云多或不清澈，用于水等；侧重「浑」，opaque 侧重「挡光」

entries.definition: dark and dirty, so that light hardly passes
entries.definitionCN: 又暗又脏，光线几乎透不过；比 opaque 多一层浑浊的凉意

entries.definition: impossible to get through or to understand
entries.definitionCN: 无法穿透或无法理解；比 opaque 更强调绝对不可进入

normalIntro.en: Opaque is shade made into a surface: whatever Latin opacus touched turned dark and stopped letting the light through.
normalIntro.cn: opaque 是「阴影」变成的一层表面：拉丁语 opacus 碰到什么，什么就变暗、不再透光。

normal.en: The -que ending is pronounced like k, as in unique.
normal.cn: 词尾 -que 发作 k 音，就像 unique 一样。

normal.en: The noun opacity keeps the same stem with -ity.
normal.cn: 名词 opacity 用同一个词干加 -ity。

normal.en: The usual opposites are transparent and clear.
normal.cn: 常见的反义词是 transparent 与 clear。

normal.en: It is often followed by to: opaque to light, opaque to outsiders.
normal.cn: 它常接 to：opaque to light、opaque to outsiders。

normal.en: Semi- can be added to it: semi-opaque glass.
normal.cn: 前面可以加 semi-：semi-opaque glass。

abstract.en: Picture frosted glass with a lamp glowing behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象磨砂玻璃后面亮着一盏灯。

abstract.en: Watch a clear stream turn brown and cloudy after rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后清澈的小溪变得又黄又浑。

abstract.en: Hold a letter written so densely that no meaning gets through.
abstract.cn: 想象拿着一封密密麻麻、看不出意思的信。

examples.en: The windows of the studio are opaque, so no one can look in.
examples.cn: 工作室的窗户是不透明的，谁也看不进去。

examples.en: His style is elegant but often opaque.
examples.cn: 他的文风优雅，但常常晦涩难懂。

examples.en: Critics said the decision was opaque and poorly explained.
examples.cn: 批评者说这个决定不透明，解释也很糟糕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧派克」——欧派克的橱窗糊了一层厚霜，从外面看不见里面，就是「不透明」；再延伸成「看不懂」；这只是一半的拼写联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 opacus（有阴影的、暗的）→ opacare（使暗）→ 法语 opaque → 英语 opaque（十五世纪作 opak，十七世纪定型），核心义「挡住光、看不清」。

sensesIntro.en: Opaque runs from blocked light to cloudy material, then to blocked meaning, blocked scrutiny, and finally the noun for the sheet that blocks light.
sensesIntro.cn: opaque 从挡住光出发，到浑浊的材料，再到挡住的含义、挡住外界的检视，最后成为指出那块挡光纸的名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: frosted glass that lets the glow through but hides what is behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：磨砂玻璃让光透过来，却藏住了后面的东西。

branches.en: The physical block on light.
branches.cn: 物理上对光线的阻挡。

branches.en: The cloudy look of a material that lost clarity.
branches.cn: 材料失去清澈后呈现的浑浊相。

branches.en: Blocked meaning in speech and writing.
branches.cn: 言语与文字中被挡住的意思。

branches.en: Blocked scrutiny of bodies and decisions.
branches.cn: 机构与决定受到的检视被挡住。

branches.en: The noun for the paper that blocks light.
branches.cn: 做成名词，指出那块挡光的纸。

intro.en: Opaque carries the Latin adjective stem opac- plus a French -que ending; English builds opacity, opaquely, and opaqueness around it.
intro.cn: opaque 带着拉丁形容词词干 opac- 与法语式词尾 -que；英语围绕它构成 opacity、opaquely 与 opaqueness。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is opacus, shady, and opacare, to darken; abstract nouns in Latin took -itas, which English turns into -ity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 opacus「有阴影的」与 opacare「使暗」；拉丁抽象名词常带 -itas，在英语里变成 -ity。

definition_zh: 光学的；视觉的；眼睛的；光学仪器部件（复数常作「光学元件」）
definition_en: relating to light, sight, or the eye, or a piece of optical equipment
core_image: 一道光穿过眼睛的瞳孔，在后脑汇成一幅清楚的画面
scene: 实验员把一块透镜装进仪器，校准镜片与眼睛之间的光路。The technician fixed a new optic onto the camera and checked the focus.
sceneCN: 这里 optic 是「光学仪器部件」（第 3 个义项：镜头一类的光学元件）；句意：技术员给相机装上一块新的光学镜片，并检查了对焦。

pos.zh: 光学的；视觉的；眼睛的
光学仪器部件；镜片（复数常指光学元件）

senses.title: Optical equipment and parts
senses.definition: relating to the design, making, or use of instruments that work with light
senses.definitionCN: 与利用光的仪器之设计、制作或使用有关的
senses.example: The lab ordered a set of optic components for the laser.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室订购了一套用于激光器的光学元件。
senses.why: Greek optos means seen or visible, so anything acting on light for the eye sits at the core of this sense.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 optos 意为「被看见的」，凡是为眼睛处理光的器件都落在这个核心义上。

senses.title: Of sight or the eye
senses.definition: connected with seeing or with the structure of the eye
senses.definitionCN: 与看东西或眼睛结构有关的
senses.example: Damage to the optic nerve can blur vision.
senses.exampleCN: 视神经受损会让视力变模糊。
senses.why: Because the eye is the organ that receives what is seen, the same root easily shifts from light to the eye itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为眼睛正是接收「被看见之物」的器官，同一个词根很容易从光转到眼睛本身。

senses.title: A piece of optical equipment
senses.definition: a lens or another part of an optical instrument
senses.definitionCN: 透镜或光学仪器上的一个部件
senses.example: He wiped the optic before putting the camera away.
senses.exampleCN: 他把相机收起来之前擦了擦镜片。
senses.why: Today the equipment sense is mostly written as the plural optics, not as a count noun in the singular.
senses.whyCN: 今天的「设备部件」义通常写成复数 optics，而不是用单数 optic 作可数名词。

senses.title: The eye itself
senses.definition: a playful or medical word for the eye and its structure, chiefly as the plural optics
senses.definitionCN: 对眼睛及其结构的戏称或医学用语，多写作复数 optics
senses.example: Slang speakers talk about the optics when they mean the eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 口语里人们用 optics 这个词来指眼睛。
senses.why: Because this word names whatever serves sight, the eye can be named by it in informal and medical styles.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词泛指为视觉服务的事物，眼睛在口语和医学语体里也能用它来代称。

senses.title: The field of optics
senses.definition: the branch of physics that studies light and vision, written as optics
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中研究光与视觉的分支学科，写作 optics
senses.example: Optics explains why a straw looks bent in water.
senses.exampleCN: 光学解释了为什么吸管在水里看起来是弯的。
senses.why: The plural optics became a field name in the seventeenth century, exactly as physics and mathematics did.
senses.whyCN: 复数 optics 在十七世纪成为学科名称，其方式与 physics、mathematics 相同。

intro.en: Optic comes from Greek optikos, of sight, which grew from the verb to see, and reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: optic 来自希腊语 optikos（关于视觉的），源自意为「看见」的动词，经拉丁语和法语传入英语。

items.en: A reconstructed root often linked with this family means to see or look, and it is shared with Latin oculus, the eye.
items.cn: 一般认为，这一词族可追溯到表示「看见、注视」的重构词根，与拉丁语 oculus（眼睛）同源。

items.en: Greek verbs for seeing and looking lead to optos, meaning seen or visible.
items.cn: 希腊语中表示「看见」和「注视」的动词派生出 optos，意为「被看见的」。

items.en: The adjective optikos means of sight or of vision, and is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: 形容词 optikos 意为「视觉的」，是英语 optic 的直接来源。

items.en: Scholarly Latin adopts the Greek adjective as opticus, of seeing.
items.cn: 学术拉丁语把这一希腊形容词借为 opticus，意为「关于看的」。

items.en: Medieval French optique carries the term into the language of learning.
items.cn: 中世纪法语 optique 把这一术语带入学术语言。

items.en: English uses optic for the eye and the nerves of sight, and later for optical equipment and the science of light.
items.cn: 英语以 optic 指眼睛和视觉神经，后来又指光学设备与光学这门学问。

note.en: Optic names the sense of sight and belongs to the large eye family, next to optical, optics, and the near meanings of seeing.
note.cn: optic 表示「视觉」，属于「眼睛」这一大词族，与 optical、optics 以及表示「看」的近义词相邻。

entries.definition: relating to light or to the sense of sight
entries.definitionCN: 光学的；视觉的（optic 加 -al 构成的常用形容词）

entries.definition: the scientific study of light and vision
entries.definitionCN: 光学（学科名称）

entries.definition: a person who makes or fits glasses
entries.definitionCN: 眼镜商；视光师

entries.definition: relating to the eye
entries.definitionCN: 眼睛的；目视的

entries.definition: relating to seeing or to the appearance of things
entries.definitionCN: 视觉的；可视的

entries.definition: relating to light particles and their technology
entries.definitionCN: 光子学的；与光粒子技术有关的

normalIntro.en: Optic lives in the eye family: the same Greek root gives optical, optics, and optician.
normalIntro.cn: optic 生活在「眼睛」词族里：同一个希腊词根还给出 optical、optics 和 optician。

normal.en: The optic nerve carries signals from the eye to the brain.
normal.cn: optic nerve 是把信号从眼睛送到大脑的视神经。

normal.en: Fibre optic cables use light instead of electricity.
