normal.cn: fibre optic 光缆用光信号代替电信号。

normal.en: Optics is the field name, like physics and mathematics.
normal.cn: optics 是学科名，和 physics、mathematics 一样用复数形式。

normal.en: An optician grinds and fits lenses for customers.
normal.cn: optician 为顾客打磨并装配镜片。

normal.en: Compare optical: optical is the everyday adjective for light and sight.
normal.cn: 对比 optical：optical 是表示「光、视觉」的日常形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a beam entering a lens and leaving as a sharp point.
abstract.cn: 想象一束光进入透镜后，出来时收成一个清晰的亮点。

abstract.en: See a pupil opening wide to catch the light.
abstract.cn: 想象瞳孔张得很大去接住光。

abstract.en: Think of a camera body with one bright glass eye on its front.
abstract.cn: 想象一台相机机身正面装着一只明亮的玻璃眼睛。

examples.en: Doctors checked the optic nerve after the accident.
examples.cn: 事故后医生检查了视神经。

examples.en: The building runs a fibre optic network to every lab.
examples.cn: 这栋楼向每间实验室铺设了光纤网络。

examples.en: Students of optics study how lenses bend light.
examples.cn: 学光学的人研究透镜如何让光偏折。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥普替」——眼科医生反复提醒「奥」秘的瞳孔要好好保「替」护；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 optos（被看见的）+ -ikos（形容词后缀）→ optikos（视觉的）→ 拉丁语 opticus → 法语 optique → 英语 optic，核心义「与看见有关」。

sensesIntro.en: Optic starts from the act of seeing, passes to the eye and its nerves, then to the instruments and the science that serve sight.
sensesIntro.cn: optic 从「看」这个动作出发，转到眼睛和视神经，再转到为视觉服务的光学仪器与光学学科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam of light passing through a lens into the eye.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束光穿过透镜进入眼睛。

branches.en: Optical equipment is the technical sense closest to Greek origin.
branches.cn: 光学设备是与希腊语原义最近的技术义项。

branches.en: Sight and the eye name the organ of vision.
branches.cn: 视觉与眼睛用来指称视觉器官。

branches.en: A lens is the physical part that the eye looks through.
branches.cn: 镜片是眼睛透过看东西的实体部件。

branches.en: The plural field name grows from the equipment sense.
branches.cn: 复数的学科名由设备义成长而来。

branches.en: The slang eye and the field name both extend the idea of serving sight.
branches.cn: 戏称「眼睛」与学科名都延伸了「为视觉服务」这一想法。

intro.en: Optic is built on the Greek stem opt- for sight, which also shapes optical, optics, and optician, and on the noun suffix -ic.
intro.cn: optic 建立在希腊语词根 opt-（看、视觉）之上，并加上名词性后缀 -ic；同一词根还构成 optical、optics 与 optician。

latinIntro.en: The Latin siblings are Greek loans such as opticus from optikos; the Greek verb optomai, to see, is the older source that lies behind them.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁同族多为来自希腊语的借词，如由 optikos 借入的 opticus；更早的来源是希腊语动词 optomai（看见）。

items.example: The root opt- appears in every member of the eye family.
items.exampleCN: 词根 opt- 出现在「眼睛」词族的每个词里。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns a root into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 把词根变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix -al gives optical.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 optical。

items.example: The suffix -ian gives optician.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ian 构成 optician。

items.example: Optical instruments focus light.
items.exampleCN: optical 指光学仪器这类词里的「光学」。

items.example: Optics is taught in the physics department.
items.exampleCN: optics 指光学学科。

items.example: An optician measures eyes for glasses.
items.exampleCN: optician 指为顾客配镜的人。

items.example: The optic nerve connects the eye and the brain.
items.exampleCN: optic nerve 连接眼睛与大脑。

items.example: Fibre optic links carry the fastest internet.
items.exampleCN: fibre optic 指光纤连接。

definition_zh: 乐观；乐观主义；乐观情绪；乐观的理由
definition_en: hopefulness and confidence that the future will be good
core_image: 太阳从地平线升起，一个人仰起头走向前，相信前面总有光
scene: 经济数据不好，团队却仍相信来年会好起来。Despite the tough year, the team kept a cautious optimism about the next season.
sceneCN: 这里 optimism 是「乐观情绪」（第 1 个义项：相信事情会好转）；句意：尽管这一年很难，团队对下一季仍抱有谨慎的乐观。

pos.zh: 乐观；乐观主义；乐观情绪；乐观的理由

derivatives.zh: 动词词干 optim- 加施事后缀 -ist，义为「乐观的人」
词干加后缀 -istic，义为「乐观的」
由 optimistic 加 -ally 构成，义为「乐观地」
同源派生，来自拉丁语 optimus（最好的），义为「最优的」

senses.title: Hope that things will turn out well
senses.definition: a feeling that the future will be good or that things will improve
senses.definitionCN: 对未来会变好或事情会改善的感觉
senses.example: There is real optimism about the new vaccine.
senses.exampleCN: 人们对新疫苗抱有真正的乐观。
senses.why: The Latin root optimus means best, so optimism is the habit of expecting the best outcome.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 optimus 意为「最好的」，因此乐观就是期待最好结果的习性。

senses.title: A philosophical doctrine
senses.definition: the philosophy that this is the best of all possible worlds, linked to Leibniz
senses.definitionCN: 认为这是所有可能世界中最好世界的哲学主张，与莱布尼茨相连
senses.example: Leibniz expressed philosophical optimism in his essays.
senses.exampleCN: 莱布尼茨在其论文中表达了哲学上的乐观主义。
senses.why: When thinkers turned the everyday hope into a doctrine in the eighteenth century, the same word became a label for a philosophy.
senses.whyCN: 十八世纪思想家把日常的期待提升为学说，同一个词便成了哲学标签。

senses.title: Grounds for hope
senses.titleCN: 乐观的理由；可乐观之处
senses.definition: a sign or fact that gives reason to expect a good outcome
senses.definitionCN: 让人有理由期待好结果的迹象或事实
senses.example: The new figures offer some optimism for investors.
senses.exampleCN: 新的数据给投资者带来了一些乐观的理由。
senses.why: Because the noun can name feelings, it also names the evidence that produces them.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个名词能指情感本身，也就能指产生这种情感的证据。

senses.title: Optimism in economics
senses.titleCN: 经济乐观情绪；市场预期
senses.definition: a general market mood in which people expect growth or rising prices
senses.definitionCN: 普遍预期增长或价格上涨的市场情绪
senses.example: Consumer optimism usually lifts retail sales.
senses.exampleCN: 消费者乐观情绪通常会推高零售额。
senses.why: Economic reports borrow the everyday feeling of hope and turn it into a measurable market sentiment.
senses.whyCN: 经济报道借用日常的「希望」之意，把它变成可测量的市场情绪。

intro.en: Optimism was coined in France in the eighteenth century from Latin optimum, the best, as the name of Leibnizian philosophy.
intro.cn: optimism 于十八世纪在法国由拉丁语 optimum（最好的）造出，最初是莱布尼茨哲学的名称。

items.en: Optimus is the superlative of bonus, good, and means best.
items.cn: optimus 是 bonus（好的）的最高级，意为「最好的」。

items.en: The noun optimum means the best thing, and stays in the same family.
items.cn: 名词 optimum 意为「最好的东西」，属于同一词族。

items.en: Writers of the Enlightenment make optimisme the name of a philosophy linked to Leibniz.
items.cn: 启蒙运动时期的作者用 optimisme 作为与莱布尼茨相连的哲学名称。

items.en: English takes optimism from French, first as a controversial doctrine.
items.cn: 英语从法语吸收 optimism，起初指一种有争议的学说。

items.en: Optimism drops the philosophy and becomes the everyday habit of hoping for the best.
items.cn: optimism 逐渐淡去哲学色彩，变成日常期待好结果的习性。

note.en: Optimism shares the Latin stem optim- with optimal and optimum, and sits next to hope and confidence in meaning.
note.cn: optimism 与 optimal、optimum 共享拉丁词干 optim-，在语义上则与 hope、confidence 相邻。

entries.definition: a person who expects good things
entries.definitionCN: 乐观的人

entries.definition: expecting good things to happen
entries.definitionCN: 乐观的

entries.definition: best or most favourable
entries.definitionCN: 最优的；最有利的

entries.definition: a feeling that what is wanted may happen
entries.definitionCN: 希望；盼望

entries.definition: a feeling that you can rely on something or someone
entries.definitionCN: 信心；把握

entries.definition: the habit of expecting bad things to happen
entries.definitionCN: 悲观；悲观主义

normalIntro.en: Optimism is built on optim-, the Latin stem for the best, with the same idea behind optimum and optimal.
normalIntro.cn: optimism 建立在 optim- 这个表示「最好」的拉丁词干上，optimum 与 optimal 背后是同一个想法。

normal.en: An optimist expects good things; an optimistic person is hopeful.
normal.cn: optimist 是乐观的人，optimistic 是乐观的。

normal.en: Cautious optimism is hope mixed with care.
normal.cn: cautious optimism 是掺入谨慎的希望。

normal.en: Blind optimism ignores the risks entirely.
normal.cn: blind optimism 是完全无视风险的乐观。

normal.en: The Latin optimum means the best, so optimism is expecting the best.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 optimum 意为「最好的」，所以乐观就是期待最好。

normal.en: Pessimism is its Latin opposite in shape and meaning.
normal.cn: pessimism 在构形和意义上都是它的反面对应词。

abstract.en: Picture a sunrise over a road that looks open ahead.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳从一条看起来一直敞开的路的前方升起。

abstract.en: See a shareholder hoping for a green chart on the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象股东盯着屏幕盼着图表变绿。

abstract.en: Think of a smiling child running toward a birthday cake.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑着奔向生日蛋糕的孩子。

examples.en: Many economists expressed optimism about the recovery.
examples.cn: 许多经济学家对复苏表示乐观。

examples.en: His optimism helped the team survive a difficult season.
examples.cn: 他的乐观帮助球队熬过了一个艰难的赛季。

examples.en: Optimists tend to recover faster from bad news.
examples.cn: 乐观的人往往更容易从坏消息中恢复。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥普体」——每天保持乐观的「体格」，好事自然来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 bonus（好的）的最高级 optimus（最好的）→ optimum（最好的东西）→ 法语 optimisme → 英语 optimism，核心义「相信会得到最好的」。

sensesIntro.en: Optimism begins as an inner hope for good results, then becomes a named philosophy, then the evidence behind hope, and finally a market mood.
sensesIntro.cn: optimism 先是内心对好结果的期待，再成为被命名的哲学学说，随后指支撑期待的证据，最后成为一种市场情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sunrise ahead, with someone walking toward it.
core.cn: 核心意象：前方日出，有人朝着光走。

branches.en: Everyday hope is the main sense.
branches.cn: 日常的希望是主要义项。

branches.en: The doctrine turns hope into a system.
branches.cn: 哲学学说把希望变成一套体系。

branches.en: Grounds for hope are the evidence behind the feeling.
branches.cn: 乐观的理由是情感背后的证据。

branches.en: Hopes and signs of hope share the same optimistic outlook.
branches.cn: 希望与希望的迹象共享同一种乐观前景。

branches.en: A market mood is the public form of private hope.
branches.cn: 市场情绪是私人希望的公共形式。

intro.en: Optimism uses the Latin stem optim- for the best, the noun suffix -ism, and the connecting vowel -i-; optimist and optimistic grow from the same stem.
intro.cn: optimism 使用表示「最好」的拉丁词干 optim-，加上名词后缀 -ism 与连接元音 -i-；optimist 与 optimistic 由同一词干长出。

latinIntro.en: Latin optimus, the best, and its noun optimum are the direct Latin members of this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 optimus（最好的）及其名词 optimum 是这个词族在拉丁语中的直接成员。

items.example: The stem optim- comes from the Latin superlative.
items.exampleCN: 词干 optim- 来自拉丁语最高级。

items.example: The suffix -ism makes a belief a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 把信念变成名词。

items.example: The vowel -i- links the stem and suffix.
items.exampleCN: 元音 -i- 连接词干与后缀。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms optimist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 optimist。

items.example: The suffix -istic forms optimistic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -istic 构成 optimistic。

items.example: An optimist sees the way out.
items.exampleCN: optimist 指乐观的人。

items.example: Optimistic people keep trying.
items.exampleCN: optimistic 表示乐观的。

items.example: Optimal comes from the same Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: optimal 来自同一拉丁词干。

definition_zh: 最适宜的；最佳的；最佳条件；最适宜程度
definition_en: the best possible, or the best set of conditions for something
core_image: 温度计的指针正好停在设备刻度盘的绿区中央
scene: 温室里蔬菜长得最好，温度和湿度都停在刻度盘正中间。Growers keep the greenhouse at the optimum for tomatoes.
sceneCN: 这里 optimum 是「最适宜程度」（第 1 个义项：最佳条件）；句意：种植者把温室保持在番茄最适宜的状态。

pos.zh: 最适宜的；最佳的
最适宜条件；最佳程度；最适值

derivatives.zh: 拉丁词干 optim- 加 -al，义为「最优的」，与 optimum 作形容词时近义
加动词后缀 -ize，义为「使最优化」
由 optimize 加名词后缀 -ation，义为「优化；最优化」
加前缀 sub-（低于），义为「次优的」

senses.title: The best conditions
senses.titleCN: 最适宜条件；最适宜程度
senses.definition: the conditions or amount that give the best possible result
senses.definitionCN: 能带来最好结果的条件或数量
senses.example: The optimum for this yeast is around thirty degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 这种酵母的最适温度约在三十度左右。
senses.why: The Latin noun optimum means the best, so the word names the peak point where results are greatest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 optimum 意为「最好的」，因此这个词指结果最好的那个峰值点。

senses.title: Best possible
senses.definition: used as an adjective for the most favourable thing or level
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词，表示最有利的、最好的
senses.example: The doctor advised the optimum dose.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议了最适宜的剂量。
senses.why: English speakers reused the noun as a modifier in the nineteenth century, producing the adjective use.
senses.whyCN: 英语使用者在十九世纪把这个名词拿来作定语，由此产生形容词用法。

senses.title: The best value in science
senses.definition: the value of a variable that gives the highest or the most efficient result, technical use
senses.definitionCN: 使结果最好或效率最高的变量取值，属技术用法
senses.example: Charts on the screen show a clear optimum in the curve.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕上的图表显示曲线上有一个明显的最适值。
senses.why: Statistics and engineering name the peak of a curve the optimum, borrowing the idea of the best point.
senses.whyCN: 统计学与工程学把曲线的峰值称作最适值，借用的就是「最佳点」这个想法。

senses.title: Best in everyday figures
senses.titleCN: 最合适的数目；最适水准
senses.definition: the figure or level that suits a purpose best, as in the optimum number of staff
senses.definitionCN: 最适合某项用途的数字或水准，如最合适的人员数量
senses.example: The firm found the optimum number of staff for the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 公司找到了夜班最合适的人员数量。
senses.why: Once a word for the peak, it is naturally applied to everyday choices such as staff numbers or batch sizes.
senses.whyCN: 一个原本表示峰值的词，自然被用到人员数量、批量大小这类日常选择上。

intro.en: Optimum is a Latin noun meaning the best, adopted into scientific English in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: optimum 是拉丁语名词，意为「最好的东西」，十九世纪被科学英语借用。

items.en: Bonus means good, and its superlative optimus means best.
items.cn: bonus 意为「好的」，其最高级 optimus 意为「最好的」。

items.en: The neuter noun optimum names the best thing or the best state.
items.cn: 中性名词 optimum 指「最好的东西」或「最好的状态」。

items.en: British writers on science borrow optimum for the best measurable condition.
items.cn: 英国科学写作者借用 optimum 表示可测量的最佳条件。

items.en: Optimum spreads from biology into engineering and statistics.
items.cn: optimum 从生物学扩散到工程学与统计学。

items.en: Optimum is now used as an adjective as often as a noun.
items.cn: 如今 optimum 作形容词与作名词的频率相当。

note.en: Optimum shares the Latin stem optim- with optimism and optimal, and sits next to best and ideal in meaning.
note.cn: optimum 与 optimism、optimal 共享拉丁词干 optim-，在语义上与 best、ideal 相邻。

entries.definition: best or most favourable
entries.definitionCN: 最优的；最有利的（形容词形式更常用）

entries.definition: to make something as good as possible
entries.definitionCN: 使最优化；优化

entries.definition: the belief that things will be good
entries.definitionCN: 乐观；乐观主义

entries.definition: the best possible standard
entries.definitionCN: 理想的；理想标准

entries.definition: the highest point of a level or curve
entries.definitionCN: 峰值；最高点

entries.definition: below the best possible level
entries.definitionCN: 次优的；未达最优的

normalIntro.en: Optimum keeps the Latin superlative meaning best, and its plural is the likewise Latin optima.
normalIntro.cn: optimum 保留拉丁语最高级「最好」的意思，其复数同样是拉丁形式的 optima。

normal.en: The optimum temperature is the one that works best.
normal.cn: optimum temperature 指效果最好的那个温度。

normal.en: Optimum can be a noun and an adjective.
normal.cn: optimum 既能作名词也能作形容词。

normal.en: Optimal is the adjective most writers prefer.
normal.cn: optimal 是多数写作者更偏爱的形容词形式。

normal.en: To optimize is to push a system toward its optimum.
normal.cn: optimize 就是把系统推向它的 optimum。

normal.en: The Latin plural is optima, and optimums also appears.
normal.cn: 拉丁语复数作 optima，英语化的写法 optimums 也有出现。

abstract.en: Picture a meter needle resting in the green band.
abstract.cn: 想象仪表的指针正好停在绿色区间里。

abstract.en: See a sunlit curve on a chart reaching its highest point.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条被照亮的曲线到达最高点。

abstract.en: Think of a recipe with exactly the right heat, time, and salt.
abstract.cn: 想象一份火候、时间、盐量都恰到好处的食谱。

examples.en: The engine runs best at its optimum speed.
examples.cn: 发动机在其最佳转速下运行得最好。

examples.en: Researchers are still looking for the optimum treatment.
examples.cn: 研究人员仍在寻找最适宜的治疗方案。

examples.en: Well-placed lights can bring out the best in a room.
examples.cn: 布置恰当的灯光能把房间衬托到最佳状态。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥普提姆」——把「奥」秘的配方「普」及各处，结果最「提」升、最理想；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 bonus（好的）的最高级 optimus（最好的）→ 中性名词 optimum（最好的东西）→ 英语 optimum，核心义「处在最优的那个点」。

sensesIntro.en: Optimum starts as the best set of conditions, then works as a modifier, then narrows in science to the best value, and finally names best everyday figures.
sensesIntro.cn: optimum 先指最佳条件，再作修饰语，随后在科学语境中收窄为最适值，最后指日常最合适的数目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle resting exactly in the middle of the green band.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针正好停在绿色区间的中央。

branches.en: Best conditions are the root noun sense.
branches.cn: 最佳条件是名词的根本义项。

branches.en: Best possible is the adjective use.
branches.cn: 最佳的、最优的是形容词用法。

branches.en: The best value is the technical peak sense.
branches.cn: 最适值是技术上的峰值义项。

branches.en: The conditions and their adjective form share the same best level.
branches.cn: 条件义与其形容词形式共享同一个最佳水平。

branches.en: A peak value and best everyday figures are both the right amount.
branches.cn: 峰值与日常合适数目都指恰到好处的量。

intro.en: Optimum is the Latin superlative stem optim- with the neuter ending -um; optimal, optimize, and optimization build on the same stem.
intro.cn: optimum 是拉丁语最高级词干 optim- 加中性词尾 -um；optimal、optimize 与 optimization 都建立在同一词干上。

latinIntro.en: Latin optimus, best, and optimum, the best thing, are the direct Latin members of this family; bonus, good, is the base of the comparison.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 optimus（最好的）和 optimum（最好的东西）是这个词族在拉丁语中的直接成员；其比较的原级则是 bonus（好的）。

items.example: The stem optim- carries the superlative idea.
items.exampleCN: 词干 optim- 携带最高级含义。

items.example: The ending -um makes optimum a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -um 使 optimum 成为名词。

items.example: The suffix -al forms optimal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 optimal。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms optimize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 optimize。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms optimization.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 optimization。

items.example: Optimal is the preferred adjective.
items.exampleCN: optimal 是更常用的形容词。

items.example: Engineers optimize the system.
items.exampleCN: optimize 指工程师优化系统。

items.example: Optimization saves fuel.
items.exampleCN: optimization 指优化过程。

items.example: The prefix sub- forms suboptimum.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 构成 suboptimum。

definition_zh: 验光师；配镜师
definition_en: a person whose job is to test eyesight, prescribe glasses or contact lenses, and check the eyes for health problems
core_image: 一间挂着镜片架的小诊室里，有人把仪器对准你的眼睛测视力
scene: 母亲觉得黑板上的字越来越模糊，于是带孩子去了街角的眼镜店。The optometrist measured the young patient sight with a row of lenses and wrote out a prescription.
sceneCN: 这里 optometrist 是「验光师」（第 1 个义项：用仪器检查视力并开配镜处方的人）；句意：验光师用一排镜片测量男孩的视力，并开出配镜处方。图中可辨识物件：验光仪器、镜片架、处方单。

pos.zh: 验光师；配镜师

collocations.zh: 验光师与配镜师（常被混淆的两个身份）

derivatives.zh: optometr- 加名词后缀 -y 构成，义为「验光学；验光师职业」
optometr- 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「验光的；与视力测量有关的」
optometric 再加 -al 构成的少见形容词，义为「测量视力的」
optometrical 加 -ly 构成，义为「以验光的方式」

senses.title: A person who tests eyesight and prescribes lenses
senses.definition: an eye care professional who measures how well a person sees and writes prescriptions for glasses or contact lenses
senses.definitionCN: 测量人的视力好坏并为眼镜或隐形眼镜开处方的人
senses.example: The optometrist put a heavy frame on my nose and clicked new lenses into it.
senses.exampleCN: 验光师把一副沉重的镜架架在我鼻梁上，不断咔嗒一声换上新镜片。
senses.why: Greek optos means seen or visible and metron means measure, so an optometrist is literally one who measures what the eye can see.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 optos 意为「可见的」，metron 意为「尺度」，所以 optometrist 本义就是「测量眼睛能看到什么的人」，测量视力正是这个词的骨。

senses.title: The professional who checks eye health
senses.titleCN: 检查眼部健康的专业人士
senses.definition: the same professional, seen as one who screens for diseases of the eye and refers serious cases to a doctor
senses.definitionCN: 同时筛查眼部疾病、并把重症转介给眼科医生的眼保健专业人员
senses.example: The optometrist shone a light into the eye to check the retina was healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 验光师用光照射眼底，检查视网膜是否健康。
senses.why: Because the same lens instruments that measure vision can also reveal the inside of the eye, the measurer of sight grew into a screener of eye disease.
senses.whyCN: 测量视力所用的镜片仪器恰好也能看到眼底，于是「测视力的人」自然扩展成「筛查眼病的人」，这是测量动作本身的延伸。

senses.title: The trained specialist as a profession
senses.definition: a licensed occupation that requires years of training in optics and is regulated by law in many places
senses.definitionCN: 需要多年视光学训练、并在许多地区受法律监管的一种持照职业
senses.example: She trained as an optometrist and now runs a practice in a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 她接受验光师培训，如今在一个小镇经营自己的诊所。
senses.why: The suffix -ist always names a role, so the word naturally becomes the name of a career and of an official title, not just a task.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ist 标记身份，词义便从「做这件事」延伸到「以这件事为业」，所以它同时是职业名称和头衔。

senses.title: The person who fits and sells the lenses
senses.definition: a person who, after the eye test, adjusts frames and lenses to fit and hands them to the patient
senses.definitionCN: 在验光之后调整镜架镜片、使其贴合脸部并把眼镜交给患者的人
senses.example: The optometrist adjusted the nose pads so the new glasses would not slide.
senses.exampleCN: 验光师调整了鼻托，让新眼镜不会往下滑。
senses.why: The prescription written by the measurer has to be turned into a real pair of glasses, so the measuring role absorbed the fitting and dispensing role as well.
senses.whyCN: 测量者写下的处方必须变成一副真实的眼镜，于是「测量」的角色顺带吸收了「调整与交付」的角色，义项由此长出。

senses.title: The eye expert consulted in everyday life
senses.definition: the eye specialist that an ordinary family turns to when a child rubs the eyes too often or an adult cannot read small print
senses.definitionCN: 当孩子频繁揉眼或大人看字模糊时，普通家庭求助的眼科专家
senses.example: Her teacher noticed the squinting and told her parents to see an optometrist.
senses.exampleCN: 老师注意到她眯眼看书，便让她父母带她去看验光师。
senses.why: Once the word names the person, it also becomes the social go-to figure for any problem with seeing, which is a cultural sense beyond the technical task.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指称一个人，它就变成「看东西出问题时想到的那个人」，这是超越技术任务的社会义项。

senses.title: The optometrist as recorded in the word book
senses.definition: the common noun as listed with British and American pronunciations and with its plural form
senses.definitionCN: 一般名词，词书同时收录英式与美式读音，并列复数形式
senses.example: The wordbook lists the noun under the letter o and gives its plural ending.
senses.exampleCN: 词书把这个名词列在字母 o 之下，并给出它的复数词尾。
senses.why: Because the word is long and Greek-built, word books record two stresses, and both are treated as correct.
senses.whyCN: 这个长词由希腊构件拼成，英美两种读法并存，词书把它们都当作正确读音。

senses.title: The measuring of sight as an idea
senses.definition: the act or field of measuring vision, seen as a science with its own instruments and standards
senses.definitionCN: 测量视力这一行为或领域，被视为有自身仪器与标准的科学
senses.example: The clinic bought new equipment to measure sight, with a digital chart and a new lens set.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所买来新的测视力设备，包括数字视力表和一套新镜片。
senses.why: The Greek root metron asks for a measuring system, so the task behind the person grows into a discipline with charts, units and tools.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 metron 本身就是「尺度」，所以人背后的那个动作会成长为一门带视力表、单位与工具的学科，这是从人回退到事的义项。

intro.en: Optometrist is a modern English coinage that glues Greek optos, meaning seen, to metron, meaning measure, with the role suffix -ist added.
intro.cn: optometrist 是现代英语造词，把希腊语 optos（可见的）与 metron（尺度）粘合，再加上表示身份的后缀 -ist。

items.en: Optos means seen or visible, and opsis means sight.
items.cn: 希腊语 optos 意为可见的，opsis 意为视觉。

items.en: Metron means a measure, the source of the -meter words.
items.cn: 希腊语 metron 意为尺度，是 -meter 类词的源头。

items.en: French optométrie names the measuring of vision as a science.
items.cn: 法语 optométrie 把视力测量确立为一门科学。

items.en: Optometrist appears as the name of the person who measures sight.
items.cn: optometrist 作为「测量视力的人」在美式英语中出现。

items.en: Laws divide optometrists from ophthalmologists by training and by surgery rights.
items.cn: 法律按训练背景与手术权限把验光师与眼科医生区分开。

items.en: The noun is standard in shops, clinics, and health systems across the English-speaking world.
items.cn: 这个名词如今在英语世界的眼镜店、诊所与医疗体系中通用。

note.en: Optometrist is a Greek-built job name, so its family sits beside sight words such as optic and optician, and beside the medical word ophthalmologist.
note.cn: optometrist 是用希腊语构件造出的职业名，它的词族与 optic、optician 这类「视觉」词相邻，也与 ophthalmologist 这类医学词相邻。

entries.definition: the science of measuring eyesight
entries.definitionCN: 测量视力的学科；验光学

entries.definition: connected with the eye or with sight
entries.definitionCN: 与眼睛或视觉有关的

entries.definition: a person who makes and sells glasses
entries.definitionCN: 配镜师；眼镜商；与 optometrist 同取 opt- 词根，但词尾来自拉丁语 opticus

entries.definition: a doctor who treats eye diseases and can perform eye surgery
entries.definitionCN: 诊治眼病并可以做眼科手术的医生；只是概念相近，词源完全不同

entries.definition: the branch of medicine that deals with eye diseases
entries.definitionCN: 眼科学，研究眼病的医学分支；只是领域相关，词源与希腊语 ophthalmos 有关

entries.definition: a place where glasses are made and fitted
entries.definitionCN: 制作与安装眼镜的店铺；只是分工相近，不是同义词

normalIntro.en: Optometrist is a crafted word: one part means to see, one part means to measure, and the ending means the person who does it.
normalIntro.cn: optometrist 是一个拼装词：一部分表示「看」，一部分表示「量」，词尾表示做这件事的人。

normal.en: The Greek element opt- shows up in optics and optical, all about sight.
normal.cn: 希腊词素 opt- 出现在「optics」和「optical」里，都与视觉有关。

normal.en: The element metron gives measure, as in thermometer and barometer.
normal.cn: 词素 metron 给出「量」，如同「thermometer」和「barometer」中的 -meter。

normal.en: The ending -ist marks a person, like dentist or pharmacist.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ist 标记一个人，如同「dentist」和「pharmacist」。

normal.en: Compare optician, which mostly sells and makes glasses, while optometrist tests eyes.
normal.cn: 对比「optician」：它主要卖眼镜、做眼镜，而验光师负责查眼睛。

normal.en: Compare ophthalmologist, a medical doctor who may cut into the eye.
normal.cn: 对比「ophthalmologist」：那是可以动眼科手术的医生。

abstract.en: Picture a row of glass lenses clicking in front of one eye, each turn measuring sight.
abstract.cn: 想象一排玻璃镜片在一只眼睛前咔嗒更换，每换一次就在测量视力。

abstract.en: Imagine a bright chart of letters shrinking line by line while a stranger holds a small paddle.
abstract.cn: 想象一张明亮的字母表一行行变小，而陌生人手里举着小板。

abstract.en: Think of a shop window with frames in rows and an eye chart taped to the wall behind.
abstract.cn: 想象商店橱窗里一排排镜架，里面的墙上贴着一张视力表。

examples.en: The optometrist said my eyes had changed and wrote a new prescription.
examples.cn: 验光师说我的视力有变化，开了一张新的配镜处方。

examples.en: Grandfather sees an optometrist every autumn to check his eyes.
examples.cn: 祖父每年秋天都去找验光师检查眼睛。

examples.en: Few students know the difference between an optometrist and an eye doctor.
examples.cn: 很少有学生分得清验光师和眼科医生的区别。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥普托米吹斯特」——奥妙的光，用「托米尺」量一量；这只是拆音联想，与希腊词根无关。

root: 希腊语 optos（可见的）+ metron（尺度）+ -ist（做某事的人）→ 法语 optométrie → 英语 optometrist，核心义「测量视力的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Optometrist starts from the act of measuring sight, then names the person who does it, afterwards the profession and the shop role, and finally the idea of vision measurement itself.
sensesIntro.cn: optometrist 从「测量视力」这一动作出发，指做这件事的人，再延伸到职业身份与店铺角色，最后回落到「视力测量」这件事本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an instrument aimed at one eye while a row of lenses clicks into place.
core.cn: 核心意象：仪器对准一只眼睛，一排镜片逐个咔嗒就位。

branches.en: The person who measures eyesight is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 测量视力的人是字面义项。

branches.en: Screening the eye for disease is the medical extension.
branches.cn: 筛查眼部疾病是医学上的延伸义项。

branches.en: The licensed career is the social sense.
branches.cn: 持照的职业身份是社会义项。

branches.en: Fitting glasses and being the family eye expert are the everyday senses.
branches.cn: 配镜与成为家庭的眼科求助对象是日常义项。

branches.en: The recorded word and the measuring discipline are the dictionary senses.
branches.cn: 词典记音与测量学科是词典层面的义项。

intro.en: Optometrist is built from Greek pieces, so its structure is more like a maths formula than a single root.
intro.cn: optometrist 由希腊语构件拼成，与其说有一个词根，不如说更像一条公式。

latinIntro.en: The Greek parts optos and metron reached English through Latin and French scientific vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊构件 optos 与 metron 经拉丁语与法语的科学词汇进入英语。

items.example: Opt- opens words about the eye and about light.
items.exampleCN: opt- 开启与眼睛和光有关的词。

items.example: The metr- root gives the idea of measuring.
items.exampleCN: metr- 词根给出测量的意思。

items.example: The vowel -o- joins opt- to -metr-.
items.exampleCN: 元音 -o- 把 opt- 与 -metr- 连在一起。

items.meaning: a person who does or practises
items.example: The suffix -ist turns the practice into a person.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 把这项实践变成一个人。

items.example: Optic describes the eye and its nerves.
items.exampleCN: optic 描述眼睛及其神经。

items.example: Optics studies how lenses bend light.
items.exampleCN: 光学研究镜片如何折射光线。

items.example: Optometry is the field behind the specialist.
items.exampleCN: 验光学是这位专业人士背后的领域。

items.example: The suffix -meter shares the same metron root.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -meter 共享同一个 metron 词根。

items.example: Metric keeps the pure sense of measuring.
items.exampleCN: metric 保留了纯粹的「测量」含义。

definition_zh: 奢华的；富丽堂皇的；富裕的；丰盛的
definition_en: very rich and showing wealth in a costly or showy way
core_image: 一间挂满水晶灯与金边家具的客厅，丝绸沙发堆满靠垫
scene: 婚礼办在一座旧宫殿的大厅里，来宾穿过铺着厚地毯的长廊。Long curtains of red velvet hung in every doorway of the opulent hotel.
sceneCN: 这里 opulent 是「富丽堂皇的」（第 1 个义项：陈设豪华、处处显富的景象）；句意：那家豪华酒店的每个门口都垂着红色天鹅绒长帘。图中可辨识物件：水晶灯、天鹅绒长帘、金边家具。

pos.zh: 奢华的；富丽堂皇的；富裕的；丰盛的

derivatives.zh: opulent 去 -t 加名词后缀 -ce 构成，义为「奢华；富丽；富裕」
opulent 加 -ly 构成，义为「奢华地；富丽地」
加否定前缀 in- 构成的少见词，义为「不富有的」

senses.title: Rich and richly decorated
senses.definition: having surroundings that are full of costly goods and clear signs of money
senses.definitionCN: 周围布满贵重物品、处处显出有钱的样子
senses.example: We walked through opulent corridors lined with thick carpet.
senses.exampleCN: 我们走过铺着厚地毯的豪华走廊。
senses.why: Latin ops means resources or wealth, so opulent first paints a place whose resources are so plentiful that they spill into every surface.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ops 意为「资源、财富」，所以 opulent 先描摹一个资源多到溢出每个角落的地方，富丽感正是「财富外溢」的画面。

senses.title: Wealthy as a person
senses.definition: having great wealth, especially wealth that is easy to see
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量财富，尤指财富一眼就能看出来的
senses.example: The opulent merchant kept four carriages and a whole floor of servants.
senses.exampleCN: 那位富商养着四辆马车和整整一层楼的仆人。
senses.why: When the word shifts from the decorated room to the people who own it, it names the owner of those overflowing resources.
senses.whyCN: 当修饰对象从被装饰的房间转到拥有房间的人，它便指「那些资源多到溢出来的人」，财富本身成了形容词。

senses.title: Luxurious food and plenty
senses.definition: plentiful and luxurious, said of food, drink or a feast
senses.definitionCN: 量多而奢华，用于形容食物、饮品或宴席
senses.example: The wedding ended with an opulent feast of roast lamb and peach tarts.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼以一顿烤羊肉加桃酥的丰盛宴席收尾。
senses.why: Food is the most visible form of rich resources, so the same word easily describes a table that cannot hold more.
senses.whyCN: 食物是最直观的「资源充足」形式，于是同一个词很自然用来形容一张堆到放不下的餐桌。

senses.title: Showy and overdone style
senses.definition: so rich and ornamental that it seems tasteless or excessive
senses.definitionCN: 过分华贵装饰，显得俗气或过度的
senses.example: Critics called the new building opulent, all gold leaf and no comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说新大楼过分华丽，满眼金箔却毫不舒适。
senses.why: When too many resources are poured into one place, the admiring sense turns into a judgement of waste and bad taste.
senses.whyCN: 当太多资源被堆进一个地方，赞美就转成对浪费和品味的批评，这是「溢出」过头后的反面义项。

senses.title: Richly abundant speech and colour
senses.titleCN: 华丽丰富的（语言、色彩等）
senses.definition: rich and full, said of language or appearance that is abundant in detail
senses.definitionCN: 丰富饱满，形容语言或外观细节繁多
senses.example: The novelist writes in opulent sentences that never waste a single adjective.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小说家句句华丽，却从不浪费一个形容词。
senses.why: The idea of plenty easily transfers from goods to words and colours, where abundance reads as richness rather than money.
senses.whyCN: 「充足」这个想法很容易从货物转到词语和色彩上，在多处就变成「丰富」而不是「有钱」。

senses.title: Lush and overgrown in nature
senses.definition: growing thickly and abundantly, used of plants and green places
senses.definitionCN: 生长茂密丰盛，用于植物与有绿意的地方
senses.example: The garden grew opulent with roses that climbed over the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 花园里的玫瑰攀过大门，长得繁茂浓密。
senses.why: Growth is also a kind of wealth, so the word borrows its plenty to describe living things that spill over their allotted space.
senses.whyCN: 生长本身也是一种「富足」，于是这个词把它的丰盛借给溢出边界的植物，用来形容繁茂。

senses.title: Rich in resources in general
senses.definition: rich in something valuable, such as a mineral, a colour or an idea
senses.definitionCN: 在某种有价值之物上十分丰富，如矿产、颜色或想法
senses.example: The region is opulent in silver and in old stories about it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区银矿丰富，关于它的老故事也很多。
senses.why: Latin ops also names material resources, so any place or thing holding a lot of value can be called opulent in that value.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ops 本身也指物质资源，所以任何存有大量价值之物的地点或事物，都可以说它在某方面很 opulent。

senses.title: The wealth behind the look
senses.definition: the abundance of money that such showy places and lives rest on
senses.definitionCN: 那些华丽场所与生活所依赖的金钱上的富足
senses.example: Behind the opulent stage lay a fortune built on imported sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 华丽舞台背后，是一笔靠进口蔗糖积累的财富。
senses.why: The adjective names a look, and the look always points back to a store of wealth, so a noun sense of abundance grows out of it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述的是一种外观，而外观总会指向背后的财富储备，于是名词化的「富足」义自然长出。

intro.en: Opulent comes from Latin opulentus, meaning wealthy, built on ops, the word for resources and power, and it entered English through French spelling.
intro.cn: opulent 来自拉丁语 opulentus（富有的），由 ops（资源、力量）构成，拼写经法语进入英语。

items.en: Ops names resources, means and wealth, and is related to opus, meaning work.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ops 指资源、财力和财富，并与 opus（工作）同源。

items.en: Opulentus means rich, full of resources, and is used of land and of people.
items.cn: 拉丁语 opulentus 意为富有的、资源充足的，用于土地，也用于人。

items.en: Opulentia names wealth and richness as a state.
items.cn: 拉丁语 opulentia 指财富与富足的状态。

items.en: The adjective travels into Old French with its meaning of wealthy.
items.cn: 这个形容词带着「富有的」含义进入古法语。

items.en: English borrows it and uses it first of rich persons and lands.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，最初用于形容富有的人与土地。

items.en: The sense widens to mean showy and over-decorated surroundings.
items.cn: 词义扩展为形容华丽、装饰过度的环境。

note.en: Opulent sits beside its family members opulence and opulently, and beside near neighbours such as affluent, lavish and sumptuous.
note.cn: opulent 与同族的 opulence、opulently 相邻，也与 affluent、lavish、sumptuous 这些近邻相邻。

entries.definition: great wealth shown in a showy way
entries.definitionCN: 炫示出来的巨大财富；奢华

entries.definition: in a rich and showy manner
entries.definitionCN: 奢华地；富丽地

entries.definition: the Latin noun for wealth
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示财富的名词，是这个词的源头

entries.definition: having plenty of money
entries.definitionCN: 富裕的；侧重「钱多」，词源来自拉丁语「流动」，与 opulent 词源不同

entries.definition: very generous and expensive
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨奢侈的；侧重「花得毫不吝惜」，词源来自古法语「倾注」

entries.definition: costly and splendid, especially of a meal or cloth
entries.definitionCN: 华贵精美的，多用于饮食与织物；词源来自拉丁语「开销」

normalIntro.en: Opulent is built on Latin ops, resources, so the adjective always points to a store of wealth behind the look.
normalIntro.cn: opulent 建立在拉丁语 ops（资源）之上，所以这个词总指出外观背后的财富储备。

normal.en: The root ops gives resource and wealth, and it is related to opus, meaning work.
normal.cn: 词根 ops 给出「资源、财富」，并与表示「工作」的 opus 同源。

normal.en: The adjective suffix -ent means being in that condition, so opulent means being full of resources.
normal.cn: 形容词后缀 -ent 表示「处于某种状态」，所以 opulent 意为「充满资源的」。

normal.en: The noun is opulence, found in phrases about great wealth.
normal.cn: 名词形式是「opulence」，常出现在表示巨额财富的说法里。

normal.en: An opulent lifestyle is a little more literary and judging than a rich lifestyle.
normal.cn: 「an opulent lifestyle」比「a rich lifestyle」更书面，也略带评判。

normal.en: Compare sumptuous, which praises the finish of cloth or food, not the size of the fortune.
normal.cn: 对比「sumptuous」：它赞美织物或食物的精致，而不是财富的规模。

abstract.en: See a golden room where every chair has a cushion and every wall has a mirror.
abstract.cn: 想象一间金色的屋子，每把椅子都有软垫，每面墙都镶着镜子。

abstract.en: Picture a table that bends under silver dishes while servants stand three deep.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被银盘压弯的餐桌，旁边站了三排仆人。

abstract.en: Think of a silk curtain that costs more than the whole house behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅比它身后整座房子还贵的丝绸窗帘。

examples.en: They rented an opulent flat for the wedding photographs.
examples.cn: 他们租了一间豪华公寓拍婚礼照片。

examples.en: The opulent dinner left half the dishes untouched.
examples.cn: 那顿丰盛得夸张的晚餐有一半菜都没动。

examples.en: His tastes were modest, though the office around him was opulent.
examples.cn: 尽管他身边的办公室富丽堂皇，他的口味却很朴素。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧普伦特」——欧式的富丽，普通人走进去也像换了身份；这只是谐音联想，与拉丁词根 ops 无关。

root: 拉丁语 ops（资源、财富；与 opus「工作」同源）→ opulentus（富有的）→ 古法语 → 英语 opulent，核心义「资源满溢」。

sensesIntro.en: Opulent starts from wealth overflowing into visible decoration, then spreads to wealthy owners, lavish food, showy excess, rich language, lush plants, abundant resources and finally the wealth itself.
sensesIntro.cn: opulent 从「财富溢出成可见装饰」出发，再扩及富有的主人、奢华的饮食、过度的炫耀、华丽的语言、繁茂的植物、丰富的资源，最后回到财富本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room so full of gold and velvet that the furnishings almost spill over.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间金与天鹅绒多到快溢出来的房间。

branches.en: Richly decorated surroundings are the core adjective sense.
branches.cn: 装饰华丽的场所是核心形容词义项。

branches.en: Calling a person wealthy moves the adjective from room to owner.
branches.cn: 形容人富裕，是把形容词从房间转到主人身上。

branches.en: Lavish food is wealth made edible.
branches.cn: 奢华的饮食是可入口的财富。

branches.en: Showy excess and rich language show the same plenty used for judgement.
branches.cn: 炫耀性的过度与华丽语言，都是同一种丰盛被用来做评价。

branches.en: Lush growth, resource wealth and wealth itself widen plenty beyond money.
branches.cn: 繁茂生长、资源丰富与财富本身，让「丰盛」越过金钱的边界。

intro.en: Opulent rests on the Latin base op-, seen in ops and opulentus, with the adjective suffix -ent added.
intro.cn: opulent 以拉丁语词基 op- 为核心，见 ops 与 opulentus，加上形容词后缀 -ent。

latinIntro.en: Latin ops means resources and wealth, and its adjective opulentus means rich.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ops 意为资源与财富，其形容词 opulentus 意为富有的。

items.example: The op- base carries the idea of plentiful means.
items.exampleCN: op- 词基承载「财力充足」的意思。

items.example: Ops is the noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: ops 是整个词族背后的名词。

items.example: Opus is related to ops through the idea of what work brings.
items.exampleCN: opus 与 ops 借「工作所带来的东西」这一想法相连。

items.meaningCN: 处于……状态的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ent makes opulent an adjective of condition.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ent 使 opulent 成为状态形容词。

items.meaningCN: 状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ence builds opulence from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ence 从形容词构成 opulence。

items.example: The suffix -ly gives the adverb opulently.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 给出副词 opulently。

items.example: The prefix in- builds the rare word inopulent.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成少见的 inopulent。

items.example: Opulence names the state the adjective describes.
items.exampleCN: opulence 命名形容词所描述的状态。

items.example: Opulent keeps the sense of costly plenty.
items.exampleCN: opulent 保留「贵重而充足」的含义。

definition_zh: 演讲；致辞；演说
definition_en: a formal speech given on a special public occasion
core_image: 一个人站在台上，用手势对着黑压压的听众大声讲话
scene: 毕业典礼上，老校长走上讲台，台下的学生安静下来。The head teacher delivered a short oration about the future of the graduating class.
sceneCN: 这里 oration 是「致辞、演说」（第 1 个义项：正式场合发表的演讲）；句意：校长就毕业班的未来发表了一段简短的致辞。图中可辨识物件：讲台、麦克风、礼堂。

pos.zh: 演讲；致辞；演说

derivatives.zh: orat- 加表示人的后缀 -or 构成，义为「演说家；雄辩者」
orator 加 -ical 构成，义为「演说术的；雄辩的」
由 oration 逆构而成的动词，义为「高谈阔论地演讲」
oration 加 -ist 构成的罕见词，义为「擅长演说的人」

senses.title: A formal public speech
senses.definition: a formal speech made in public on a special or solemn occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在特殊或庄重场合公开发表的正式讲话
senses.example: He delivered the oration at the opening of the new library.
senses.exampleCN: 他在新图书馆落成仪式上发表了演说。
senses.why: The Latin verb orare means to speak or plead before an assembly, so an oration is speech turned into a public ceremony.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 orare 意为「在集会面前说话、陈情」，所以演说就是把说话变成一场公开仪式，正式感来自「面向众人」这一点。

senses.title: The speech of praise and mourning
senses.definition: a set speech of praise or of grief, especially one given for a dead person or a great cause
senses.definitionCN: 赞扬或哀悼的成套讲话，尤指为逝者或伟大事业所发的
senses.example: The oration over the fallen soldier moved everyone in the square.
senses.exampleCN: 为阵亡士兵所作的悼词感动了广场上的所有人。
senses.why: Ancient practice paired formal speaking with funerals and with the praise of great deeds, so grief and praise became the earliest content of the oration.
senses.whyCN: 古代的正式演说常与葬礼和对伟业的赞颂相配，于是哀悼与歌颂成了演说最早的内容，这一义项就长在「正式场合」上。

senses.title: The skill of the skilled speaker
senses.definition: the art or style of speaking impressively in public, judged by gesture, voice and structure
senses.definitionCN: 在公众面前打动人地讲话的技艺或风格，以手势、声音与结构来评判
senses.example: Her oration, learned from ancient teachers, swept the crowd like a current.
senses.exampleCN: 她那种师承古人的雄辩，像一阵水流扫过人群。
senses.why: Once the form is fixed, the manner of performing it calls for training, so the word also names the craft of the speaker rather than the text.
senses.whyCN: 形式一旦固定，表演它的方式就需要训练，于是这个词也指演说者的技艺而不是讲稿，这是从成品到能力的转移。

senses.title: The written text of a speech
senses.definition: the written words of a formal speech, kept for print, record or study
senses.definitionCN: 正式演说的文字稿，用于印刷、存档或研究
senses.example: The old oration is printed in full at the back of the book.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇古老的演说词全文印在书后的附录里。
senses.why: When speeches were written down and passed on, the event shrank into a document, and the paper kept the name of the speech.
senses.whyCN: 当演说被写下并传递，事件就收缩成一份文件，纸面上的文字仍沿用了演讲的名字，义项由此固定。

senses.title: A speech to persuade or plead
senses.titleCN: 陈情；劝说性的公开讲话
senses.definition: a public appeal intended to persuade listeners to act or to grant something
senses.definitionCN: 旨在劝说听众采取行动或答应某事的公开呼吁
senses.example: The farmer gave a short oration for a fairer price for milk.
senses.exampleCN: 那位农夫作了一段简短的陈情，要求给牛奶一个更公平的价格。
senses.why: Orare also means to plead, so the speaker standing before a crowd was first imagined as asking for something, which gives the persuasive sense.
senses.whyCN: orare 还有「恳求」之义，站在人群前的说话者最初就被想象成在「求一件事」，劝说性的义项由此而来。

senses.title: Grandeloquent speech that seems empty
senses.definition: long and lofty speech that sounds impressive but says little, used as a mild criticism
senses.definitionCN: 听起来堂皇却言之无物的长篇讲话，用作温和批评
senses.example: We sat through an oration about duty that lasted nearly an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 我们耐着性子听了一段近一小时的关于责任的长篇大论。
senses.why: When the formal style is imitated without the occasion, the same word turns negative and names speech whose weight is all performance.
senses.whyCN: 当没有相应场合却模仿那种正式腔调，同一个词就转向反面，用来指「重量全在表演上」的讲话。

senses.title: The act of speaking in assembly
senses.definition: the act of addressing an assembled group, as a piece of procedure rather than a performance
senses.definitionCN: 向聚集的人群讲话的行为，视作程序性环节而非表演
senses.example: The council waited for the oration to end before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 议会等那段陈述结束后才进行表决。
senses.why: The noun can also step back and name the event itself, the moment of addressing a body, which is why it appears in rules of procedure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能退后一步，指「向一个群体讲话的时刻」这件事本身，所以它会出现在议事规则里，这是从结果回看动作。

senses.title: The rhetorical form of the classical example
senses.titleCN: 古典修辞中的演说体裁
senses.definition: a recognised kind of speech in classical rhetoric, with its own sections and rules of style
senses.definitionCN: 古典修辞学中一种被承认的演讲体裁，有固定的段落与文体规则
senses.example: Students copied the oration of a Greek writer to learn its shape.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们抄写一位希腊作家的演说，以学习它的结构。
senses.why: Greek and Roman teachers turned speaking into a school subject, and the oration became the textbook object with a fixed beginning, middle and end.
senses.whyCN: 希腊罗马的教师把说话变成学科，演说就成为教科书里的对象，有了固定的开头、中段与结尾，这个义项是教育制度的产物。

intro.en: Oration goes back to Latin oratio, a telling or speaking, from the verb orare, to speak, plead or pray.
intro.cn: oration 上溯到拉丁语 oratio（讲述、说话），出自动词 orare（说话、恳求、祈祷）。

items.en: Orare means to speak before others, to plead, and also to pray.
items.cn: orare 意为在他人面前讲话、恳求，也表示祈祷。

items.en: Oratio names the act of speaking, and so a speech or a style of speech.
items.cn: oratio 指说话的行为，因而也指讲话或讲话方式。

items.en: Orator is the speaker, the man trained to plead in court or in assembly.
items.cn: orator 指说话的人，是在法庭或集会中受训陈词的人。

items.en: The form reaches Old French, which carries a formal speech or plea.
items.cn: 该词形进入古法语，带有正式讲话或陈情的含义。

items.en: Middle English uses oration for a formal speech and for a prayer.
items.cn: 中古英语用 oration 指正式演说，也指祈祷。

items.en: The word narrows to solemn public speeches and to the study of rhetoric.
items.cn: 词义收窄为庄重的公开演说，并用于修辞学研究。

note.en: Oration belongs to the Latin speaking family around orare, so it sits beside orator and oratory, and near everyday speech words such as speech and address.
note.cn: oration 属于围绕 orare 的拉丁「说话」词族，与 orator、oratory 相邻，也与 speech、address 这些日常说法相邻。

entries.definition: a person who is good at making formal speeches
entries.definitionCN: 擅长正式演说的人；演说家

entries.definition: the art of public speaking
entries.definitionCN: 演说术；雄辩术

entries.definition: a priest or shrine said to speak for a god
entries.definitionCN: 神谕与传神谕者；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a talk given to an audience
entries.definitionCN: 对听众所作的讲话；最中性的说法，不强调隆重

entries.definition: a formal speech made to a group
entries.definitionCN: 正式向群体发表的讲话；词源来自拉丁语「使靠近」

entries.definition: a talk given by a priest as part of worship
entries.definitionCN: 布道；宗教场合的讲道；只是场景相关，词源来自拉丁语「谈话」

normalIntro.en: Oration grows out of the Latin verb orare, to speak or plead, and the -tion ending turns the act into a thing.
normalIntro.cn: oration 长自拉丁语动词 orare（说话、恳求），后缀 -tion 把动作变成一样东西。

normal.en: The base orat- also gives the person, the orator, who performs it.
normal.cn: 词基 orat- 还给出做这件事的人，即「orator」。

normal.en: The ending -tion often names an act or a product, as in action from act.
normal.cn: 后缀 -tion 常命名动作或成品，如同从「act」到「action」。

normal.en: Deliver an oration is the standard verb, not make one.
normal.cn: 说「deliver an oration」，而不是「make one」，搭配要记牢。

normal.en: An oration is loftier than a speech, and far longer than a toast.
normal.cn: oration 比 speech 更庄重，也比祝酒词长得多。

normal.en: Compare peroration, the closing part of a speech, built on the same base.
normal.cn: 对比「peroration」：演说的收尾段落，用的是同一个词基。

abstract.en: See a single figure on a stone step, arms raised, before a sea of hats.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在石阶上，举起双臂，面前是一片帽海。

abstract.en: Hear a hall go silent as the speaker waits three whole seconds before speaking.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅在演说者开口前的三秒停顿中完全安静下来。

abstract.en: Picture a black and white photograph of a man at a lectern, one hand on his chest.
abstract.cn: 想象一张黑白照片：男子立在讲台后，一只手按在胸前。

examples.en: The mayor ended the ceremony with a brief oration on civic duty.
examples.cn: 市长以一段关于公民责任的简短演说结束了典礼。

examples.en: His orations were famous for their long, rolling sentences.
examples.cn: 他的演说以冗长而起伏的句子闻名。

examples.en: She wrote the oration weeks before the ceremony.
examples.cn: 她在典礼前几周就写好了这篇演说词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦雷神」——他一开口，像雷神般镇住全场；这只是谐音联想，与拉丁词根 orare 无关。

root: 拉丁语 orare（讲话、恳求、祈祷）→ oratio（说话；演说）→ 古法语 → 英语 oration，核心义「在众人面前正式讲话」。

sensesIntro.en: Oration starts from the formal speech as an event, then the praise and grief it carries, the skill behind it, the written text, its persuasive and empty versions, the act itself, and finally the classical form.
sensesIntro.cn: oration 从「正式演说」这一事件开始，再延伸到它承载的赞美与哀悼、背后的技艺、写成的文稿、劝说与空洞的两种变体、说话的行为本身，最后到古典修辞中的体裁。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one speaker on a raised step, facing an assembled crowd in silence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在台阶高处，面对安静聚集的人群。

branches.en: The formal public speech is the core sense.
branches.cn: 正式的公开演说是核心义项。

branches.en: Praise and mourning give the speech its earliest content.
branches.cn: 赞美与哀悼赋予演说最早的内容。

branches.en: The skill and the written text are the two faces of the same speech.
branches.cn: 技艺与文稿是同一场演说的两个面。

branches.en: Persuasion, empty grandeur and the bare act all come from public speaking.
branches.cn: 劝说、空洞的堂皇与纯粹的说话行为，都来自公开讲话。

branches.en: The classical school form is the final, fixed sense.
branches.cn: 古典学校的体裁是最后固定下来的义项。

intro.en: Oration is built from the Latin base orat-, which names speaking, plus the noun suffix -ion.
intro.cn: oration 由表示「说话」的拉丁词基 orat- 加上名词后缀 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin orare means to speak, plead or pray, and oratio is the act of speaking.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 orare 意为说话、恳求、祈祷，oratio 指说话的行为。

items.example: The orat- base carries the act of speaking aloud.
items.exampleCN: orat- 词基承载「出声讲话」这个动作。

items.example: Orare gives the family its voice.
items.exampleCN: orare 为词族提供「声音」。

items.example: Oratio turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: oratio 把动词变成名词。

items.meaningCN: 动作或其结果的名称后缀
items.example: The suffix -ion builds oration from the base.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 从词基构成 oration。

items.example: The suffix -or gives orator, the person.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 给出 orator，即那个人。

items.example: The suffix -ory gives oratory, the art or the chamber.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ory 给出 oratory，指技艺或小堂。

items.meaningCN: 以某种方式行动的动词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ate back-forms the verb orate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 逆构出动词 orate。

items.example: The prefix per- builds peroration, the closing part.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 per- 构成 peroration，即收尾部分。

items.example: Peroration shares the whole family base.
items.exampleCN: peroration 共享整族的词基。

definition_zh: 兰花；兰花科植物；淡紫色；兰花奖
definition_en: a plant with showy flowers and unusually shaped petals, or the pale purple colour of many of its blossoms
core_image: 一朵花瓣左右对称、中间托着唇瓣的兰花，像一只停住的小虫
scene: 博物馆的玻璃温室里忽然安静下来，参观者围着一株垂下的花枝拍照。The new orchid in the glasshouse smells like vanilla and candy.
sceneCN: 这里 orchid 是「兰花」（第 1 个义项：有奇特花形的兰科观赏植物）；句意：温室里那株新兰花闻起来像香草和糖果。可想见画面：玻璃穹顶、垂下的花枝、停下的脚步声。

pos.zh: 兰花；兰科植物；淡紫色
兰花的；淡紫色的

derivatives.zh: 由 orchid 加拉丁后缀 aceous 构成，义为「兰科的；兰花状的」
由 orchid 加 ology 构成，义为「兰花学」，专门研究兰科植物的学科
由 orchidology 去掉词尾加 ist 构成，义为「兰花研究者」
由 orchid 加 ist 构成，义为「兰花栽培爱好者」

senses.title: The flowering plant
senses.definition: a plant of a large family with brightly coloured flowers and one odd petal in the middle
senses.definitionCN: 兰科的一种植物，花鲜艳，中间有一片形状特别的唇瓣
senses.example: The greenhouse keeps hundreds of tropical orchids.
senses.exampleCN: 温室里养着几百株热带兰花。
senses.why: Greek orchis named the plant by its round, paired underground tubers, and the image of two little testicles grew into the whole flower.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 orchis 先按地下的两个圆形块茎给这种植物起名，那对「小东西」的形象后来扩展到整株花。

senses.title: A pale purple colour
senses.definition: a pale or vivid purple colour, like the blossoms of many orchids
senses.definitionCN: 类似许多兰花花朵的淡紫色或鲜艳紫色
senses.example: She chose a dress in soft orchid for the spring party.
senses.exampleCN: 她为春日晚会挑了一条柔和的兰紫色连衣裙。
senses.why: Once the flower became famous for its colours, the colour itself took the name of the flower.
senses.whyCN: 这种花因颜色出名之后，颜色本身也就借用了花的名字。

senses.title: The wild plant of meadows and woods
senses.definition: a wild orchid growing in grassland or woodland, often small and easy to miss
senses.definitionCN: 生长在草地或林地里的野生兰花，常常很小、容易被错过
senses.example: A single wild orchid stood alone in the wet meadow.
senses.exampleCN: 湿草地上孤零零立着一株野兰。
senses.why: Cultivated orchids are showy, but the family also lives wild in temperate meadows and woods.
senses.whyCN: 栽培兰花艳丽夺目，但这一科也有许多种类野生于温带草地和林地。

senses.title: The tree-dwelling epiphyte
senses.definition: a tropical orchid that grows on the branches of trees, holding on by thick roots
senses.definitionCN: 热带兰花，粗壮的气生根扒住树枝生长
senses.example: The orchid clings to the trunk with aerial roots.
senses.exampleCN: 这株兰花用气生根紧紧扒住树干。
senses.why: The Greek word meant testicle, and the word for the tree-dweller came from an Englishman who mistook its twin tubers for the body part.
senses.whyCN: 希腊原词本指睾丸，而表示树上附生者的这个词，来自一位英国人把成对的假鳞茎误认成虫子的形状。

senses.title: An exotic, fragile beautiful thing
senses.titleCN: 珍稀之物；娇艳难得的人或物
senses.definition: something or someone treated as rare, delicate, and costly, like a glasshouse flower
senses.definitionCN: 被当作稀有、娇贵、昂贵的人或物，如同温室里的花
senses.example: Her voice was an orchid among the plain notes of the choir.
senses.exampleCN: 在合唱团朴素的嗓音中，她的声音像一朵兰花。
senses.why: The orchid needs special care and a high price, so the flower became a metaphor for rare beauty.
senses.whyCN: 兰花需要精心照料、价格高昂，于是这朵花成了「珍稀之美」的比喻。

senses.title: The Greek root sense
senses.definition: the botanical root of the word refers to the rounded tubers of certain ground orchids
senses.definitionCN: 词源上先指某些地生兰的圆形块茎
senses.example: The Greek plant name pointed to the tubers of the root.
senses.exampleCN: 希腊语的植物名指向根部的块茎。
senses.why: In Greek, orchis meant both the plant and the round tuber under it, so the root sense stays attached to the word.
senses.whyCN: 在希腊语里，orchis 既指这种植物，也指它地下的圆形块茎，所以词根义一直附着在这个词上。

senses.title: The plant family and its hybrids
senses.definition: any member of the orchid family, including the many cultivated hybrids of modern gardens
senses.definitionCN: 兰科的任何成员，包括现代园艺中大量培育的杂交品种
senses.example: Gardeners cross two species to breed a new orchid.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁把两个品种杂交，培育出新兰花。
senses.why: Botany groups several thousand species under one family name, and breeders keep adding hybrids to it.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把数千个物种放进同一个科，育种者又不断把杂交品种加进来。

senses.title: An award given for quality
senses.definition: a prize or badge named after the flower and given for some kind of excellence
senses.definitionCN: 以兰花命名、颁发给某种卓越表现的奖项或标志
senses.example: The film won an orchid at the regional contest.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片在地区比赛中获得了一座兰花奖。
senses.why: Because the flower stands for rare beauty, clubs and festivals use its shape as a symbol of high quality.
senses.whyCN: 因为兰花象征稀有之美，俱乐部和节庆便把它的形状当作高品质的象征。

intro.en: Orchid goes back to Greek orchis, the name of the plant, chosen for its round paired tubers.
intro.cn: orchid 可追溯到希腊语 orchis（兰属植物），这个名字取自它成对的圆形块茎。

items.en: Orchis names both the plant and its round tuber.
items.cn: orchis 既指这种植物，也指它圆形的块茎。

items.en: Botanists adopt Orchis as the genus name.
items.cn: 植物学家把 Orchis 借来作属名。

items.en: Early writers spell the plant name orchidion or orchis.
items.cn: 早期作者把植物名写作 orchidion 或 orchis。

items.en: Orchid enters common use after the London Botanical Society has a spelling dispute.
items.cn: 伦敦植物学会就拼写争执之后，orchid 进入通用词汇。

items.en: Cultivation and colour names spread orchid into gardens and dye charts.
items.cn: 栽培业和颜色名称把 orchid 带进园艺和色卡。

note.en: Orchid is a flower name of Greek origin, close to orchis and orchidaceous, and to other celebrated blossom names.
note.cn: orchid 是源自希腊语的花名，与 orchis、orchidaceous 以及其它著名的花名相邻。

entries.definition: the genus name and the older form of the plant name
entries.definitionCN: 兰属的属名，也是这种花名较早的写法

entries.definition: belonging to the orchid family
entries.definitionCN: 兰科的；兰花状的

entries.definition: the study of orchids
entries.definitionCN: 兰花学

entries.definition: a tall plant with large trumpet-shaped flowers
entries.definitionCN: 百合，另一种著名的观赏花

entries.definition: the flower of a plant, especially one that has opened
entries.definitionCN: 花；花朵，泛指开花的部分

entries.definition: a rounded underground part from which many flowers grow
entries.definitionCN: 鳞茎；球茎，许多花卉植物的地下部分

normalIntro.en: Orchid is a Greek plant name that was once spelled orchis and became fashionable with Victorian collectors.
normalIntro.cn: orchid 是希腊语植物名，早期写作 orchis，维多利亚时代的收藏热潮让它流行起来。

normal.en: The word keeps the ch of the old spelling orchis, not a k sound alone.
normal.cn: 这个词保留了旧拼写 orchis 中的 ch，而不是单发 k 音。

normal.en: The adjective orchidaceous describes anything belonging to the orchid family.
normal.cn: 形容词 orchidaceous 描述属于兰科的内容。

normal.en: Growers of the flower are called orchidists in old books.
normal.cn: 旧书里把种兰花的人称为 orchidists。

normal.en: An orchid grower needs shade, damp air, and a steady hand.
normal.cn: 兰花种植者需要遮阴、湿润的空气和稳定的手。

normal.en: Compare lily and orchid: both are showy plants, but only the orchid has a middle lip.
normal.cn: 对比 lily 与 orchid：两者都是艳丽的花，但只有兰花有中间的唇瓣。

abstract.en: Think of a butterfly that has settled on a stem and grown roots.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蝴蝶落在茎上，然后长出了根。

abstract.en: Picture a paint chip in soft mauve, so pale the colour needs the flower to name it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张淡紫的色卡，浅到只能借花的名字来叫它。

abstract.en: See a small wild stem hiding in wet grass.
abstract.cn: 想象湿草里藏着一根小小的野兰花茎。

examples.en: The orchid on the windowsill reopened in the warm season.
examples.cn: 窗台上的兰花在温暖的季节又重新开花了。

examples.en: Botanists have described thousands of orchid species.
examples.cn: 植物学家已经描述过数千种兰花。

examples.en: Her favourite colour is a pale orchid that suits her dark hair.
examples.cn: 她最喜欢的颜色是淡兰紫，很衬她的黑发。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦可惜」——花期太短，养兰的人常叹一声「哦可惜」；仅供联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 orchis（兰属植物；块茎）→ 拉丁语 orchis（属名）→ 英语 orchis，后改写为 orchid；核心义「成对的圆形块茎长出的对称花朵」。

sensesIntro.en: Orchid starts with the plant named for its paired tubers, then lends its name to a pale purple, to wild and tree-dwelling kinds, and finally to rare beauty and awards.
sensesIntro.cn: orchid 先指因数对块茎得名的兰科植物，再把名字借给淡紫色，又扩及野生种与附生种，最后指稀有之美和奖项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flower with two side petals like wings and a middle lip below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一朵两侧花瓣如翅、中央垂下唇瓣的花。

branches.en: The named plant itself is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 得名的植物本身是最日常的义项。

branches.en: A colour borrows the flower name.
branches.cn: 颜色借用了花的名字。

branches.en: Wild kinds grow where the cultivated ones never go.
branches.cn: 野生种类生长在栽培兰花去不了的地方。

branches.en: Tree-dwellers and hybrids are branches of the same family.
branches.cn: 附生种与杂交品种是同一科的不同分支。

branches.en: Rare beauty grows into awards and personal metaphors.
branches.cn: 稀有之美引申出奖项与对人的比喻。

intro.en: Orchid is built on the Greek plant word orchis, with English forms such as -aceous, -ology, and -ist attached to it.
intro.cn: orchid 建立在希腊语植物词 orchis 之上，英语为它接上 aceous、ology、ist 等词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek plant name orchis directly, and botany kept that form as a genus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语直接借用希腊语植物名 orchis，植物学把它保留为属名。

items.example: Orchis gives the plant its first name.
items.exampleCN: orchis 给这种植物起了最初的名字。

items.example: Orchis stays as the botanical genus name.
items.exampleCN: Orchis 保留为植物学属名。

items.example: Orchid is the everyday English form.
items.exampleCN: orchid 是日常使用的英语形式。

items.example: Orchids is the regular plural.
items.exampleCN: orchids 是常规复数。

items.meaning: belonging to, of the nature of
items.example: The suffix -aceous forms orchidaceous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -aceous 构成 orchidaceous。

items.example: Orchidaceous names the family.
items.exampleCN: orchidaceous 表示兰科。

items.example: The suffix -ology forms orchidology.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ology 构成 orchidology。

items.meaning: a person who does or practises
items.example: The suffix -ist forms orchidist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 orchidist。

items.meaning: a grower or lover of orchids
items.meaningCN: 兰花栽培者；兰花爱好者
items.example: Orchidist names a hobbyist.
items.exampleCN: orchidist 指兰花爱好者。

definition_zh: 组织；机构；团体；组织工作；安排；体系
definition_en: a group of people who work together for a purpose, or the act of arranging things into an ordered whole
core_image: 许多零件被依次装进同一个机壳，各自咬合，只为一个用途
scene: 大厅里，志愿者把写有名字的牌子逐一挂上墙，椅子按组摆成几圈。The charity organisation raised enough money for a new shelter.
sceneCN: 这里 organisation 是「组织、机构」（第 1 个义项：为共同目的而运作的一群人及其团体）；句意：这家慈善机构筹到了足够的钱建一座新收容所。可想见画面：大厅、名牌、排成圈的椅子。

pos.zh: 组织；机构；团体；组织（工作）；安排；条理

derivatives.zh: 由 organisation 加 al 构成，义为「组织的；组织方面的」
organisation 的动词基形，义为「组织；筹备；安排」
由 organise 加 -er 构成，义为「组织者；筹备者」
organisation 的美式拼写，释义相同

senses.title: A body of people with a purpose
senses.definition: a group of people, such as a company, club, or charity, that works together for a common aim
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目标一起工作的团体，如公司、俱乐部或慈善机构
senses.example: The organisation employs forty people in three cities.
senses.exampleCN: 这个机构在三个城市雇用四十人。
senses.why: The Greek word for tool became the word for a body made of parts, and a group of people fitted to one aim is that body.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语的「工具」变成了「由部件构成的身体」，为一件事配合起来的一群人就是这副身体。

senses.title: The act of arranging
senses.definition: the process of planning and arranging people or things so that something runs well
senses.definitionCN: 规划并安排人或事物、使事情顺利运转的过程
senses.example: The organisation of the whole event took six months.
senses.exampleCN: 整场活动的组织工作花了六个月。
senses.why: The same noun can name the doing of the work, not just the body that does it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既能指做事的那群人，也能指做事这件事本身。

senses.title: Structure and order
senses.definition: the way in which the parts of a thing are put together and ordered
senses.definitionCN: 事物的各部分组合与排序的方式
senses.example: Good organisation makes the files easy to find.
senses.exampleCN: 条理清楚让文件很容易找到。
senses.why: Order built into parts is the abstract continuation of the fitting of tools into one body.
senses.whyCN: 把秩序装进各个部件，正是「把工具装进一个身体」这个意象的抽象延续。

senses.title: A system in a larger whole
senses.titleCN: 组织；系统（如国际组织的一员）
senses.definition: a system of related parts within a larger body, such as the organs of a business or a structure
senses.definitionCN: 更大整体中的相关部件系统，如企业的各部门或机构部门
senses.example: The charity has a loose organisation across five countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构在五个国家有松散的体系。
senses.why: From organs of a body the word moved to the bodies that make up a company or a community.
senses.whyCN: 从身体的「器官」出发，这个词又转指构成公司或共同体的各个机构。

senses.title: The capacity for orderly work
senses.definition: the personal ability to plan and keep things tidy and on time
senses.definitionCN: 个人规划事务、保持整洁并按时的能力
senses.example: Her organisation saved the team from a missed deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 她的条理性让团队没有错过截止日期。
senses.why: When the arranging is done by a person, the noun names the quality shown in that work.
senses.whyCN: 当安排由一个人完成时，这个名词就转而指那份工作中体现出来的品质。

senses.title: The union of workers
senses.definition: an association of workers or members formed to act together for shared interests
senses.definitionCN: 为共同利益而联合行动的劳动者或成员的协会
senses.example: The organisation of local teachers meets every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 当地教师的工会每年春天开会。
senses.why: The most common purpose of a fitted group is to bargain or act as one voice.
senses.whyCN: 这样配合起来的一群人，最常见的用途就是一起谈判、用一个声音说话。

senses.title: Planning as a subject
senses.titleCN: 组织学；组织方法（学科义）
senses.definition: the study or practice of how groups and tasks are arranged and run
senses.definitionCN: 研究群体和任务如何被安排与运作的学科或实践
senses.example: He teaches organisation and management at the college.
senses.exampleCN: 他在学院教组织与管理。
senses.why: A whole subject grows out of the verb once businesses start asking how to arrange work.
senses.whyCN: 当企业开始追问「怎样安排工作」时，科目便从动词里长了出来。

senses.title: A living body
senses.definition: a living being seen as a body made of organs working together
senses.definitionCN: 被看作由器官协同运作的身体的活物
senses.example: Each cell helps keep the organisation of the body alive.
senses.exampleCN: 每个细胞都帮助维持生物体活着。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: a body in which every part has a job.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：一副身体，每个部件各司其职。

intro.en: Organisation comes from mediaeval Latin organizare, to give a body its organs, built on organum, a tool or instrument.
intro.cn: organisation 来自中世纪拉丁语 organizare（赋予身体器官），其词基 organum 意为「工具、器具」。

items.en: Organon means a tool or instrument, from ergon, work.
items.cn: organon 意为工具或器具，源自 ergon（工作）。

items.en: Organum keeps the sense of an instrument and of a part of the body.
items.cn: organum 同时保留「器具」与「身体部位」两种意思。

items.en: Organizare means to arrange parts into a body.
items.cn: organizare 表示把部件安排成一副身体。

items.en: Organiser carries the word of arranging into French.
items.cn: organiser 把「安排」之义带进法语。

items.en: Organise and organisation arrive with the sense of arranging into a whole.
items.cn: organise 与 organisation 带着「安排成整体」的意义进入英语。

items.en: The noun widens to businesses, charities, and unions.
items.cn: 这个词扩大到企业、慈善团体和工会。

note.en: Organisation is the British spelling built on Greek organon, near organ, organist, and to the nouns institute and company.
note.cn: organisation 是建立在希腊语 organon 上的英式拼写，与 organ、organist 以及 institute、company 等名词相邻。

entries.definition: to arrange people or things into a working whole
entries.definitionCN: 把人和事安排成一个整体

entries.definition: a part of the body with a special function
entries.definitionCN: 器官；风琴

entries.definition: a person who plays the organ
entries.definitionCN: 管风琴演奏者

entries.definition: a large established body such as a university or bank
entries.definitionCN: 制度；大型机构，如大学或银行

entries.definition: a business that sells goods or services
entries.definitionCN: 公司；商号

entries.definition: an organised group of people with shared interests
entries.definitionCN: 协会；社团

normalIntro.en: Organisation is the noun of organise, and organ sits inside both as the image of parts joined for a job.
normalIntro.cn: organisation 是 organise 的名词形式，organ 嵌在两者之中，意象都是「为某项任务拼合的部件」。

normal.en: British writing keeps the s of organisation, and American writing uses a z.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留 organisation 中的 s，美式拼写则用 z。

normal.en: The adjective organisational describes everything about how a group is run.
normal.cn: 形容词 organisational 描述一个团体如何运作的各个方面。

normal.en: An organisation chart shows who reports to whom.
normal.cn: organisation chart 显示谁向谁汇报。

normal.en: Charitable organisation is a common partner in IELTS writing.
normal.cn: charitable organisation 是雅思写作中常见的搭配。

normal.en: Compare organ and organisation: one part of a body, or a body of people built like one.
normal.cn: 对比 organ 与 organisation：前者是身体的一个部件，后者是按身体构造造出来的一群人。

abstract.en: Picture a tray of gears being dropped into one casing.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘齿轮被依次放进同一个机壳。

abstract.en: Imagine a desk cleared of papers, each pile on time.
abstract.cn: 想象一张清空了纸张的桌子，每摞都刚好按时完成。

abstract.en: See a row of desks joined by the same rule.
abstract.cn: 想象一排桌子被同一条规则串起来。

examples.en: A local organisation runs free evening classes.
examples.cn: 一家当地机构开设免费的夜校课程。

examples.en: The organisation of the conference was faultless.
examples.cn: 这次会议的组织工作无可挑剔。

examples.en: She joined an international organisation after graduation.
examples.cn: 毕业后她加入了一个国际组织。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，干那件事」——大家一听「哦，干那件事」就一起上手，这就是组织；仅供联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 organon（工具）→ 拉丁语 organum（器具；器官）→ 中世纪拉丁语 organizare（把部件安排成身体）→ 法语 organiser → 英语 organise 与 organisation，核心义「把部件装成一个为某用途服务的整体」。

sensesIntro.en: Organisation begins with a body of people fitted to one aim, widens to the act of arranging, then to structure, workers unions, a subject, and the living body itself.
sensesIntro.cn: organisation 先指为一件事配合起来的一群人，再扩展为安排的动作，继而指结构、工会、学科，最后回到被组织起来的活体本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate parts clicked into one case so that the whole works.
core.cn: 核心意象：散件被依次扣进同一个机壳，整体才转得起来。

branches.en: A group fitted to one purpose is the modern headline sense.
branches.cn: 为一个目的配合起来的一群人，是今天最主要的义项。

branches.en: Arranging work is the action reading of the noun.
branches.cn: 安排工作，是这个词的动作义。

branches.en: Structure is what the arranging leaves behind.
branches.cn: 结构是安排之后留下来的形态。

branches.en: Systems inside groups and unions of workers are both sub-bodies.
branches.cn: 团体内部的系统和劳动者的工会都是下一层的组织体。

branches.en: Skill, subject, and living body show how far the word reaches.
branches.cn: 能力、学科与生物体展示了这个词延伸的距离。

intro.en: Organisation is organise plus the noun ending ation, built on the Latinised organ of instrument and body part.
intro.cn: organisation 是 organise 加上名词词尾 ation，词基 organ 由拉丁语而来，兼指器具与器官。

latinIntro.en: Latin organum means both an instrument and a part of the body, and organizare means to fit parts into a body.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 organum 既指器具，也指身体部位；organizare 表示把部件装配成身体。

items.example: Organon supplies the tool image.
items.exampleCN: organon 提供「工具」的意象。

items.meaning: an instrument, a part of the body
items.example: Organum doubles as instrument and organ.
items.exampleCN: organum 兼指器具与器官。

items.example: Organizare is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: organizare 是名词背后的动词。

items.meaning: to arrange into a working whole
items.example: Organise is the verb the noun is built on.
items.exampleCN: organise 是这个名词所依附的动词。

items.meaning: a group or the act of arranging
items.example: Organisation combines the verb with -ation.
items.exampleCN: organisation 由动词加 -ation 构成。

items.example: The suffix -ation turns organise into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 把 organise 变成名词。

items.example: The suffix -al forms organisational.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 organisational。

items.meaning: relating to the running of a group
items.example: Organisational describes how a group is run.
items.exampleCN: organisational 描述团体如何运作。

items.example: The suffix -er forms organiser.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 organiser。

items.meaning: a person who arranges an event
items.example: Organiser names the person who arranges.
items.exampleCN: organiser 指负责筹备的人。

definition_zh: 东方的；亚洲的；（宝石）有光彩的；东方品种的
definition_en: belonging to or coming from the east, especially East Asia, or of a jewel with a strong sheen
core_image: 一轮太阳从地平线东侧升起，把那一边染成金红
scene: 清晨，老城的屋顶先被阳光照亮，鸽子从东边的塔上飞起。The old merchant kept his oriental rugs rolled in a dry cupboard.
sceneCN: 这里 oriental 是「东方的、东方出产的」（第 1 个义项：来自东方的物品或风格）；句意：这位老商人把他的东方地毯卷起来存放在干燥的柜子里。可想见画面：清晨的金红色屋顶、东边高塔、飞起的鸽子。

pos.zh: 东方的；亚洲的；东方风格的；（宝石）有特殊光泽的
东方人（旧式用法，今多视为冒犯，宜避免）

derivatives.zh: 由 oriental 加 ist 构成，义为「东方学家」
由 oriental 加 -ise 构成，义为「使东方化」
由 oriental 加 ity 构成，义为「东方性；东方特色」
由 oriental 加 ness 构成，义为「东方特质」

senses.title: From the east, especially East Asia
senses.definition: belonging to or coming from the east, especially East or South East Asia
senses.definitionCN: 属于或来自东方，尤指东亚或东南亚
senses.example: The shop sells oriental ceramics and silk.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖东方瓷器和丝绸。
senses.why: Latin oriens is the rising sun, so oriental names whatever lies where the sun comes up.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 oriens 指「升起的太阳」，所以 oriental 指太阳升起那一侧的一切。

senses.title: A person from the east
senses.titleCN: 东方人（旧式称呼，今多视为冒犯）
senses.definition: a person from East Asia, a term now often felt to be offensive
senses.definitionCN: 来自东亚的人，这一称呼如今常被认为冒犯
senses.example: Modern editors avoid calling a person an oriental.
senses.exampleCN: 现代编辑避免把某人称为 oriental。
senses.why: The adjective was turned into a noun for people, lumping whole nations into one compass direction.
senses.whyCN: 形容词被拿来当人的名词，把整片民族硬塞进一个罗盘方位里。

senses.title: A jewel of high lustre
senses.definition: describing a pearl or gem of fine colour and sheen, especially one from the East
senses.definitionCN: 形容珍珠或宝石颜色与光泽上乘，尤指来自东方的
senses.example: The jeweller set three oriental pearls in the brooch.
senses.exampleCN: 珠宝匠在胸针上镶了三颗上等东方珍珠。
senses.why: The finest gems came overland from the East, so its name became a stamp of quality on any jewel.
senses.whyCN: 最好的宝石自东而西经陆路运来，于是这个名字成了宝石上的品质标记。

senses.title: Rising, as the sun
senses.definition: rising or beginning to appear, as the sun at dawn
senses.definitionCN: 上升或开始出现，如黎明时的太阳
senses.example: Painters once showed the oriental sun above a dark ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 画家曾在深色的山脊上画初升的太阳。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin sense before it became a label for a region.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语的本来意思，在它变成地域标签之前就已存在。

senses.title: The compass direction
senses.definition: relating to the east as a direction, as in an eastern wing or gate
senses.definitionCN: 与东这个方位有关，如东侧的翼楼或东门
senses.example: The oriental gate faces the morning light.
senses.exampleCN: 东门朝向晨光。
senses.why: Once the word meant the direction, it could sit before any building, wind, or road.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示方位，就能放在任何建筑、风或道路之前。

senses.title: A style in Western art and decor
senses.titleCN: 东方风格的（西方艺术中的模仿）
senses.definition: imitating or adopting eastern designs and materials in western craft
senses.definitionCN: 在西方工艺中模仿或采用东方的图案与材料
senses.example: The hotel lobby imitates an oriental style of lattice work.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店大厅模仿了东方样式的格栅。
senses.why: Western workshops copied eastern patterns and then stamped them with the direction name.
senses.whyCN: 西方工坊仿制东方纹样，再用方位名给它们贴上标签。

senses.title: The eastern type
senses.titleCN: 东方的（用于动植物品种名）
senses.definition: naming a species or variety known from eastern lands, as with the poppy or the moth
senses.definitionCN: 为见于东方的物种或品种命名，如东方罂粟或东方蛾
senses.example: An oriental poppy glowed at the end of the border.
senses.exampleCN: 花境尽头一朵东方罂粟开得火红。
senses.why: Botanists name a species after the direction where it was first collected.
senses.whyCN: 植物学家用最初采集地的方位来给物种命名。

senses.title: The eastern part of a region
senses.definition: standing for the eastern part of a country or region, as in a spoken form of eastern provinces
senses.definitionCN: 指一个国家或地区的东部，如口语中表示东部省份的说法
senses.example: News from the oriental provinces arrived late.
senses.exampleCN: 东部各省的消息很晚才到。
senses.why: Shortening eastern into oriental let speakers name a whole eastern stretch in one word.
senses.whyCN: 把 eastern 压缩成 oriental，说话人就能用一个词指整片东部。

intro.en: Oriental grows from Latin oriens, the rising sun or the east, itself from oriri, to rise.
intro.cn: oriental 源自拉丁语 oriens（升起的太阳、东方），其动词为 oriri（升起）。

items.en: Oriens is the rising sun and the direction where it appears.
items.cn: oriens 指升起的太阳，以及太阳出现的方向。

items.en: Orientalis means of the east, formed from oriens.
items.cn: orientalis 意为「东方的」，由 oriens 构成。

items.en: The adjective reaches French as oriental.
items.cn: 这个形容词以 oriental 的形式进入法语。

items.en: The word enters English for things of the east, especially gems and fabrics.
items.cn: 该词进入英语，指东方的物品，尤其是宝石与织物。

items.en: Oriental becomes the ordinary label for Asia, and scholars coin orientalist for its students.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，oriental 成了亚洲的常用标签，学者又造出 orientalist 指研究者。

items.en: Later usage marks the noun for people as dated and often offensive.
items.cn: 后来的用法把指人的名词义标为过时，并常被视为冒犯。

note.en: Oriental is the adjective of the rising sun, close to orient, origin, and arise, and to the directional words eastern and western.
note.cn: oriental 是「升起」的形容词，与 orient、origin、arise 同源，也与表示方向的 eastern、western 相邻。

entries.definition: the east, or to find ones bearings
entries.definitionCN: 东方；确定方位

entries.definition: the point where something begins or rises
entries.definitionCN: 起源；起点

entries.definition: to come into being or move upward
entries.definitionCN: 出现；升起

entries.definition: of the east, a plainer and safer word
entries.definitionCN: 东方的，更中性更常用

entries.definition: of the west
entries.definitionCN: 西方的

entries.definition: of the west, built from the word for setting sun
entries.definitionCN: 西方的，源出「落下的太阳」

normalIntro.en: Oriental shares its root with orient, origin, and arise, all resting on the Latin oriri, to rise.
normalIntro.cn: oriental 与 orient、origin、arise 同根，都建立在拉丁语 oriri（升起）之上。

normal.en: Occidental is its mirror image, built on the setting sun.
normal.cn: occidental 是它的镜像，源出「落下的太阳」。

normal.en: An orientalist is a scholar of eastern languages and cultures.
normal.cn: orientalist 指研究东方语言与文化的学者。

normal.en: Orient, meaning to find ones way, keeps the same rising image.
normal.cn: 表示「辨明方向」的 orient 保留了同一个「升起」的意象。

normal.en: Origin and arise both picture something coming up into view.
normal.cn: origin 与 arise 都描绘某物在视野中升起、出现。

normal.en: In careful writing, prefer eastern or Asian, especially for people.
normal.cn: 严谨写作中优先用 eastern 或 Asian，尤其指人时。

abstract.en: Picture a red sun sliding up over a flat horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象一轮红日从平坦的地平线上升起。

abstract.en: Imagine a traveller from that sunrise side unloading silk and pearls.
abstract.cn: 想象一位来自日出那侧的旅人卸下丝绸与珍珠。

abstract.en: See a compass needle pointing at the morning sky.
abstract.cn: 想象罗盘指针指向清晨的天空。

examples.en: The museum holds a fine collection of oriental textiles.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆收藏着精美的东方织物。

examples.en: Oriental pearls are prized for their deep colour.
examples.cn: 东方珍珠因色泽深厚而受珍视。

examples.en: Modern style guides prefer eastern or Asian for people.
examples.cn: 现代写作指南在指人时更倾向用 eastern 或 Asian。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，烈日头」——东边日头刚升起，光照得人喊「哦，烈日头」；仅供联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 oriri（升起）→ oriens（升起的太阳；东方）→ orientalis（东方的）→ 古法语 oriental → 英语 oriental；核心义「太阳升起的那一侧」。

sensesIntro.en: Oriental begins with the sunrise side, which names a region and its goods, then spreads to gems, direction, style, and finally to a dated way of naming people.
sensesIntro.cn: oriental 先指太阳升起的一侧，由它给地域与物产命名，再扩及宝石、方位、风格，最后成了一种指人的旧式说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sun coming up over the edge of the world, gilding one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳从世界的边缘升起，把一侧染成金色。

branches.en: The region where the sun rises is the main sense.
branches.cn: 太阳升起的那片地域是主要义项。

branches.en: Turning the adjective into a noun for people is the contested sense.
branches.cn: 把形容词变成指人的名词，是有争议的义项。

branches.en: Fine gems from the east carry the name as a quality mark.
branches.cn: 来自东方的上等宝石把名字当作品质标记。

branches.en: Rising and direction are the literal old senses.
branches.cn: 上升与方位是较早的字面义项。

branches.en: Style, species names, and eastern regions all borrow the compass.
branches.cn: 风格、物种名与地区东部都在借用这个方位。

intro.en: Oriental is the Latin oriens plus the adjective ending alis, with English forms such as -ist, -ise, and -ity built on it.
intro.cn: oriental 是拉丁语 oriens 加上形容词词尾 alis，英语又为它接上 ist、ise、ity 等词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin oriri means to rise, oriens is the rising sun, and orientalis means of the east.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oriri 意为升起，oriens 指升起的太阳，orientalis 意为东方的。

items.example: Oriri gives the image of the sun coming up.
items.exampleCN: oriri 提供太阳升起的意象。

items.example: Oriens names the sunrise side.
items.exampleCN: oriens 指日出那一侧。

items.example: Orientalis is the direct source of the word.
items.exampleCN: orientalis 是这个词的直接来源。

items.example: Oriental keeps the direction sense.
items.exampleCN: oriental 保留了方位含义。

items.example: The suffix -al forms the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成这个形容词。

items.meaning: to find ones bearings, or the east
items.example: Orient keeps the same root as a separate word.
items.exampleCN: orient 以另一个词的身份保留同根。

items.meaning: a person who studies or practises
items.meaningCN: 研究者或从业者的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ist forms orientalist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 orientalist。

items.example: Orientalist names a specialist.
items.exampleCN: orientalist 指专门研究者。

items.meaning: to make or cause to be
items.example: The suffix -ise forms orientalise.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 构成 orientalise。

items.example: Orientalise describes copying eastern style.
items.exampleCN: orientalise 描述仿效东方风格。

definition_zh: 确定方向；使适应；使朝向；定位
definition_en: to find or establish your position in relation to your surroundings, or to make yourself or something face or fit a particular direction or situation
core_image: 一个人站在陌生的街口，先认出东边的太阳，再转身对准要去的方向
scene: 新生第一次走进偌大的校园，手拿着地图四处张望。The guide helped the new students orientate themselves to the morning sun.
sceneCN: 这里 orientate 是「确定方位、辨明方向」（第 1 个义项：弄清自己相对于周围环境的方位）；句意为导游帮助新生们以早晨的太阳辨认方向。

pos.zh: 动词：确定方向；使适应；使朝向

collocations.zh: 确定自己的方位；熟悉环境

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「方向；定位；入学或岗前介绍」
同义动词，把动词缩写而成，义为「使适应；确定方向」
由过去分词转为形容词，义为「以……为导向的」，常作后缀套用，如 market orientated
加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「使迷失方向；使不知所措」

senses.title: To find where you are
senses.definition: to find out your position and the directions around you, especially in a new or confusing place
senses.definitionCN: 弄清自己所处的位置与周围方向，尤指在新环境或容易迷路的地方
senses.example: She stopped at the corner to orientate herself with the help of the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 她在街角停下来，借助太阳辨认方向。
senses.why: The Latin root oriens means the rising sun, and in East Asia the rising sun was the fixed point from which every other direction was named.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 oriens 意为「升起的太阳」，在东亚的先民以日出之处为固定基准来命名其他方位，所以这个词天生就是「对太阳定位」。

senses.title: To make something face a direction
senses.definition: to place or position a building, map, or object so that it faces a particular direction
senses.definitionCN: 把建筑、地图或物体摆放成朝向某个特定方向的位置
senses.example: The architects orientated the house to catch the afternoon light.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师让房子朝向能接收到午后阳光的方向。
senses.why: Once the eastern sunrise is a known direction, anything can be turned to match it, so the verb moved from finding a heading to giving something a heading.
senses.whyCN: 一旦东方日出成了已知方向，任何东西都能被转过去与它对齐，于是动词从「找到朝向」扩展为「给某物定朝向」。

senses.title: To adapt to a situation
senses.definition: to become familiar with a new place, job, or situation, or to help someone do this
senses.definitionCN: 熟悉新的地方、工作或处境，或帮助别人做到这一点
senses.example: The first week is designed to orientate new staff to office life.
senses.exampleCN: 第一周旨在帮助新员工熟悉办公生活。
