senses.why: Knowing which way you face is the first step to fitting in; a new arrival must first orientate, then settle, so the same verb came to mean helping people settle in.
senses.whyCN: 搞清楚自己面朝哪边是融入环境的第一步；新人先要定好方位，才能安定下来，于是这个动词也用来表示帮助别人融入。

senses.title: To give something a purpose or focus
senses.titleCN: 使有明确目标；使侧重于
senses.definition: to direct an activity, plan, or organisation towards a particular aim, audience, or value
senses.definitionCN: 把活动、计划或机构引向特定的目标、受众或价值
senses.example: The school orientates its courses towards practical skills.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校把课程重点放在实用技能上。
senses.why: A direction is also an aim; pointing something at a goal is the abstract version of pointing a house at the sunrise.
senses.whyCN: 方向也是目标；让某物对准某个目标，就是「让房子朝向日出」的抽象版本。

senses.title: To place yourself relative to something
senses.definition: to establish how you or a thing stands in relation to a larger group, scale, or system
senses.definitionCN: 确定自己或某物相对于更大群体、等级或系统的位置
senses.example: Readers need to orientate the article against the evidence in the earlier reports.
senses.exampleCN: 读者需要把这篇文章与先前报告中的证据对照着理解。
senses.why: A map is useless without a fixed reference, and the mind works the same way: to understand a new fact you orientate it against the facts you already hold.
senses.whyCN: 没有固定参照系的地图毫无用处，头脑也一样：要理解一个新事实，就得把它放在已有事实之间定位。

senses.title: Self-orientated: focused on oneself
senses.definition: in compounds ending in orientated, directed towards the thing named, such as self, market, or profit
senses.definitionCN: 用于以 orientated 结尾的复合词中，表示「以……为导向的」，如以自我、市场或利润为导向
senses.example: A profit orientated company still has to listen to its customers.
senses.exampleCN: 以利润为导向的公司仍然必须倾听顾客的声音。
senses.why: The past participle kept the idea of pointing at something, so in compounds orientated names the object being pointed at.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词保留了「指向某物」的意思，因此复合词里的 orientated 用来标出被指向的对象。

intro.en: Orientate comes from Latin oriens, the rising sun, through the verb oriri, to rise.
intro.cn: orientate 来自拉丁语 oriens（升起的太阳），源头是动词 oriri（升起）。

items.en: Oriri means to rise, used above all of the rising of the sun.
items.cn: oriri 意为升起，最常用于太阳升起。

items.en: Oriens, the present participle, means the rising one and stands for the east, the quarter of the sunrise.
items.cn: 现在分词 oriens 意为「正在升起的（那一位）」，进而指东方，即日出之处。

items.en: French orient names the east and passed into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 orient 指东方，十四世纪进入英语。

items.en: The verb orient is recorded in English in the early eighteenth century with the sense of finding the east.
items.cn: 英语动词 orient 在十八世纪初有记录，本义是找出东方。

items.en: The longer form orientate is modelled on French orienter; it is standard in British usage, while American usage prefers orient.
items.cn: 较长的 orientate 仿照法语 orienter 构成；英式英语视其为标准，美式英语更常用 orient。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same rising-sun family; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of finding a direction or settling in.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「日出」词族；近义组收其他表示找方向或安顿下来的说法。

entries.definition: the short verb of the same family, preferred in American English
entries.definitionCN: 同族的短动词，美式英语更常用。

entries.definition: the direction something faces or the state of being settled in a new place
entries.definitionCN: 朝向；定位；新生或新员工的情况介绍。

entries.definition: to make someone lose all sense of direction
entries.definitionCN: 使迷失方向；使不知所措。

entries.definition: to find the exact place of something, without the idea of facing
entries.definitionCN: 找到某物的确切位置，不带「朝向」的意思。

entries.definition: to plan and follow a route, usually while moving
entries.definitionCN: 规划并沿路线行进，通常是在移动中。

entries.definition: to change in order to fit new conditions, close to the settling-in sense
entries.definitionCN: 为适应新条件而改变，接近「使适应」的义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real rising-sun root and the phrases that orientate actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「日出」词根，以及 orientate 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Oriens is the rising sun in Latin: to orientate is to turn the whole body until it matches the sunrise.
normal.cn: oriens 在拉丁语中指升起的太阳：orientate 就是把整个身体转到与日出对齐的方向。

normal.en: Oriental and orientation share the same root, and both point back to the east.
normal.cn: oriental 与 orientation 同源，二者都指向「东方」。

normal.en: British usage says orientate, American usage says orient; both are correct in their own variety.
normal.cn: 英式英语说 orientate，美式英语说 orient；在各自变体里都正确。

normal.en: A building is orientated to the sun; a course is orientated to the job market.
normal.cn: 建筑被朝向太阳；课程被对准就业市场。

normal.en: Disorientate adds dis- to orientate, so losing your bearings is the opposite act.
normal.cn: disorientate 是在 orientate 前加 dis-，所以迷失方向正好是它的反义动作。

abstract.en: Stand at a crossing with a compass: the needle swings once and settles, and the whole city suddenly makes sense.
abstract.cn: 想象站在十字路口拿着指南针：指针摆动一下后停稳，整座城市忽然变得清楚了。

abstract.en: Turn a house until its windows face the morning light; the house is orientated.
abstract.cn: 把房子转到窗户都朝向晨光的位置，房子就 orientated 了。

abstract.en: A new worker with a map of the office on day one feels orientated by the end of the week.
abstract.cn: 带着办公室地图来上班的新人，到周末就觉得自己已经融入了。

examples.en: The hikers orientated themselves by the ridge of the mountain.
examples.cn: 徒步者借助山脊辨认自己的方位。

examples.en: The museum is orientated so that its main windows face the river.
examples.cn: 博物馆的朝向让主窗正对着河面。

examples.en: The course is orientated towards students who plan to work abroad.
examples.cn: 这门课程面向打算去海外工作的学生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，瑞安·特」——瑞安抬头看见日出，立刻知道自己朝哪边；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 oriri（升起）→ 现在分词 oriens（升起的太阳；东方）→ 法语 orient（东方）→ 英语 orient / orientate，核心义「对着日出的方向定位」。

sensesIntro.en: Orientate starts with the body finding east, then a building being turned to face somewhere, and finally grows into adapting to a place or aiming at a purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: orientate 从身体辨认东方开始，再指建筑被转到某个朝向，最后扩展为适应新环境和以某个目标为导向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person turns slowly until the whole face is square with the rising sun.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人慢慢转身，直到整个面庞正对升起的太阳。

branches.en: The body sense: finding where you are by a fixed point such as the sun.
branches.cn: 身体线：借助太阳这样的固定点弄清自己在哪儿。

branches.en: The object sense: turning a building, map, or device to a chosen direction.
branches.cn: 物体线：把建筑、地图或装置转到选定的方向。

branches.en: The social sense: finding your place among people, facts, or an institution.
branches.cn: 社会线：在人群、事实或机构中找到自己的位置。

branches.en: The purpose sense: aiming a plan or an organisation at a goal.
branches.cn: 目标线：让计划或机构对准某个目标。

branches.en: The compound sense: orientated names the thing that is aimed at.
branches.cn: 复合词线：orientated 用来标出被指向的对象。

intro.en: Orientate is built on a Latin rising-sun root, and its family is made with ordinary English suffixes such as -ation and dis-.
intro.cn: orientate 建立在拉丁语「日出」词根上，其词族用 -ation、dis- 等普通英语词缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin oriri, oriens and orientalis are all recorded, so the root itself is certain; only the exact birth of the English verb orientate is debated.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oriri、oriens 与 orientalis 均有文献记录，词根本身是确定的；值得讨论的只是英语动词 orientate 的准确产生年代。

items.example: The verb describes the sun coming up.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述太阳升起。

items.example: The participle is the direct source of orient.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词是 orient 的直接来源。

items.example: The adjective gives English oriental.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词构成英语 oriental。

items.example: The suffix turns orient into a longer verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 orient 拉长成另一个动词。

items.example: It forms orientation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 orientation。

items.example: The prefix forms disorientate.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀构成 disorientate。

items.example: It forms the adjective orientated.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词 orientated。

items.example: It forms oriental from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 它从同一词根构成 oriental。

items.meaning: to find or set a direction
items.example: The verb keeps the sunrise image inside it.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把日出的意象保留在里面。
